facets.facet_name: Heavenly Princess Who Chose to Return to Earth
facets.core_claim: Exiled from heaven for a broken cup, Liễu Hạnh came down by choice again and again, living among humans; she is the goddess who refuses to stay away.

facets.facet_name: Holy Mother of the Four Palaces
facets.core_claim: As Mẫu Liễu Hạnh she presides over the Four Palaces; in lên đồng mediumship she and her court descend into the mediums.

facets.facet_name: The Fourfold Cosmos of the Mother Goddesses
facets.core_claim: The Mothers of the Four Palaces divide the cosmos into sky, mountain-forest, water and earth, governing all through their spirit court.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Mountains and Forests
facets.core_claim: The green-robed Mother of the Upper Forests governs mountains, trees and creatures and blesses the people of the highlands.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Water Palace
facets.core_claim: Daughter of the Dragon King, Mẫu Thoải rules the waters of the Four Palaces and keeps boats and farmers' fields watered.

facets.facet_name: Silent Child Who Became a Giant Savior
facets.core_claim: At the nation's need the mute child grew in a moment into a giant warrior, defeated the invaders and ascended to heaven; he is one of the Four Immortals.

facets.facet_name: Deified General Who Commands the Spirit Armies
facets.core_claim: Saint Trần, victor over the Mongols, now leads the spirit hosts against demons and sickness; his temples at Kiếp Bạc and Bảo Lộc are centers of exorcism.

facets.facet_name: Kitchen Gods Who Report to Heaven
facets.core_claim: From the hearth the Táo watch the household all year and at Tết ride their carp up to the Jade Emperor to report.

facets.facet_name: Mountain Spirit Who Holds Back the Floods
facets.core_claim: Each rainy season Sơn Tinh lifts the hills against the waters of his rival, keeping the people safe.

facets.facet_name: Jilted Water Spirit of the Annual Floods
facets.core_claim: Thủy Tinh's unending jealousy brings the yearly floods of the Red River, as he tries again to seize what he lost.

facets.facet_name: Holy Mother of Nha Trang
facets.core_claim: Thiên Y A Na gave the people of the coast rice farming and weaving and protects them from her tower-temple at Nha Trang.

facets.facet_name: Guardian God of the Village Communal House
facets.core_claim: The Thành Hoàng, invested by imperial patent, watches over the village from the đình and receives its offerings and festivals.

facets.facet_name: Bathala Maykapal, Creator of All
facets.core_claim: Bathala made the world and humanity and rules from above; the anito are his intermediaries among people.
facets.scholarly_note: Spanish chroniclers reported Bathala as the highest deity; the details of his family (Apolaki, Mayari, Tala as children) come from 20th-century compilations.

facets.facet_name: Androgynous Deity of Fertile Fields
facets.core_claim: Farmers offer to Lakapati when they sow, praying that fields will yield and that the community will be fed.

facets.facet_name: One-Eyed Moon Who Shares the Sky
facets.core_claim: After her battle with Apolaki, Mayari rules the night with her one remaining eye while he rules the day.
facets.scholarly_note: The sibling-war narrative comes from 20th-century compilations; Mayari as a moon deity is reported from Tagalog and Kapampangan areas.

facets.facet_name: Sun God and Patron of Warriors
facets.core_claim: Apolaki rides across the day as the sun and gives courage to warriors; he and Mayari divide the sky between day and night.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of the Stars and Morning Star
facets.core_claim: Tala lights the stars and guides those who travel and work before sunrise.

facets.facet_name: Keeper of Kasamaan and Its Four Agents
facets.core_claim: Sitan rules Kasamaan and sends his four agents among humans to bring sickness, discord and death.
facets.scholarly_note: The name may reflect Spanish "Satanás"; the four-agent scheme comes from 20th-century compilations.

facets.facet_name: Visayan Sovereign of the Sky
facets.core_claim: Kaptan rules the sky; from his contest with the sea-lord the islands of the world were formed, and from a bamboo stalk the first man and woman emerged.

facets.facet_name: Sea Serpent That Swallows the Moon
facets.core_claim: Bakunawa's hunger causes eclipses; only the clamor of the people forces it to release the moon.

facets.facet_name: The One Unthinkable God (Acintya)
facets.core_claim: All gods are rays of Sang Hyang Widhi; as Acintya he cannot be conceived, and the empty seat at the top of the padmasana is his.

facets.facet_name: King of the Gods in Jonggringsaloka
facets.core_claim: Batara Guru sits enthroned over the Javanese heavens, ordering the world, sending gods on missions and judging their disputes.

facets.facet_name: The God Hidden in a Clown's Body
facets.core_claim: Semar's lowly, laughable form hides the eldest divinity; he serves the heroes, guards Java, and even Batara Guru must bow to his rebuke.

facets.facet_name: Rice Goddess Whose Body Became the Crop
facets.core_claim: From the grave of Dewi Sri grew rice and the food plants; she lives in every rice field and granary and must be honored at planting and harvest.

facets.facet_name: Queen of the Southern Sea and Consort of Kings
facets.core_claim: The Queen of the South Sea grants sovereignty to the Mataram kings through spiritual marriage and claims the drowned who wear her green.

facets.facet_name: Widow-Witch Queen of the Graveyard
facets.core_claim: Rangda commands the leyak and black magic, yet as a manifestation of Durga her terrible power also guards the village.

facets.facet_name: Lion Spirit Who Protects the Village
facets.core_claim: The Barong defends the village against Rangda and illness; his sacred mask is kept in the temple and brought out to purify the land.

facets.facet_name: World Serpent Beneath the Earth
facets.core_claim: From the lowest underworld Antaboga upholds the world; the cosmic turtle and the rice goddess come from him.

facets.facet_name: Devouring Giant of Time
facets.core_claim: Kala devours the unprotected; only the ruwatan performance, which tells his story and pacifies him, releases those he may claim.

facets.facet_name: Supreme God of the Upperworld (the Hornbill)
facets.core_claim: Mahatala rules the Upperworld; with Jata of the Underworld he forms the totality of the godhead, and from their encounter came the tree of life and the first humans.

facets.facet_name: Watersnake Queen of the Underworld
facets.core_claim: Jata rules the waters and the world below; with Mahatala she makes up the whole divine reality.

facets.facet_name: The Great Beginning, Creator of the Three Worlds
facets.core_claim: All beings come from Mulajadi na Bolon, who brought forth the gods of the three worlds; the Parmalim pray to him as the one God.

facets.facet_name: Holy Guardian Spirit of a Place
facets.core_claim: Each keramat watches over its locality; those who honor his shrine are protected and their requests heard.

facets.facet_name: King of the Nats, Who Descends at Thingyan
facets.core_claim: Thagyamin heads the nats as a guardian of the Buddha's religion and descends at the New Year to judge the deeds of humankind.

facets.facet_name: Royal Pantheon of Spirits Born of Violent Death
facets.core_claim: Born of tragic deaths, the nats hold great power over luck, health and the land; honored and fed, they protect, neglected, they punish.

facets.facet_name: Guardian Nat of Every Household
facets.core_claim: The burned blacksmith became the house-nat: a green coconut hung on the house pillar honors Mahagiri, who protects the family.

facets.facet_name: Mother Nat of Mount Popa
facets.core_claim: Popa Medaw reigns over Mount Popa, the home of the nats, honored by pilgrims and mediums.

facets.facet_name: Earth Goddess Who Wrung Out Her Hair
facets.core_claim: Called by the earth-touching gesture, Mae Thorani bore witness to the Buddha's merit and drowned Mara's host in the waters stored in her hair.

facets.facet_name: Spirits of Land, House and Village
facets.core_claim: The phi of each place must be honored at the spirit house; when respected they guard the household, when slighted they bring illness and misfortune.

facets.facet_name: Rice Mother Who Holds the Grain's Soul
facets.core_claim: Mae Phosop is the life in the rice; she must be treated gently and honored, or she will leave the fields and famine will follow.

facets.facet_name: Naga King of the Mekong
facets.core_claim: Phaya Nak holds the river and rain in his power and guards the Buddha's relics and the peoples of the Mekong.

facets.facet_name: Ancestral Guardians of the Land
facets.core_claim: The Neak Ta own and protect each piece of Khmer land; the community honors them so that rain falls and harm stays away.

facets.facet_name: Mother of the Cham Kingdom
facets.core_claim: Po Nagar brought the land and its riches into being and protects the kingdom from her temple on the hill at Nha Trang.

facets.facet_name: Atua of the Ocean and Its Creatures
facets.core_claim: All fish and sea creatures are the children of Tangaroa; his waves contend with Tāne's land, and his tapu governs fishing.

facets.facet_name: Atua of War and of Humankind
facets.core_claim: Tū alone withstood the storm and subdued his brothers' offspring, so that humans, his descendants, may hunt, fish, cultivate and make war.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Darkness and Disease
facets.core_claim: Whiro is the source of all evil, sickness and death; from Rarohenga he battles Tāne's light and devours the dead.

facets.facet_name: Storm Who Avenged the Parted Parents
facets.core_claim: Loyal to his father the Sky, Tāwhirimātea makes war with storm and hurricane on all his brothers who agreed to the separation.

facets.facet_name: Atua of Uncultivated Foods
facets.core_claim: Bracken root and wild food are the children of Haumia; they sustain the people in lean times.

facets.facet_name: Unborn Son Whose Stirring Shakes the Earth
facets.core_claim: Rūaumoko lives within Papatūānuku; when he moves, the land shakes and fire rises from below.

facets.facet_name: Ancestress Who Keeps Fire in Her Nails
facets.core_claim: Fire comes from Mahuika's nails; tricked by Māui, she let fire loose and hid it in the kaikōmako, māhoe and tōtara trees for humanity.

facets.facet_name: God of the Deep Ocean and Companion of Kāne
facets.core_claim: Kanaloa rules the deep sea and guides voyagers; with Kāne he walks the islands, opening fresh springs and drinking ʻawa.

facets.facet_name: Kanaloa as Leader of Rebellious Spirits (Kepelino)
facets.core_claim: In Kepelino's telling Kanaloa led the spirits in rebellion against Kāne, Kū and Lono and was cast down to the underworld.
facets.scholarly_note: This account is widely judged to reflect Christian influence on the Catholic-educated author; earlier Hawaiian practice honors Kanaloa positively.

facets.facet_name: Mother Goddess of Birth and Renewal
facets.core_claim: Haumea brings forth children and plants, taught true childbirth, and is reborn young again and again to mate with her descendants.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Underworld Lua-o-Milu
facets.core_claim: In Lua-o-Milu the unguided dead come under the rule of Milu, below the land of the living.

facets.facet_name: Sky Father and Ancestor of the Chiefs
facets.core_claim: With Papa, Wākea begot the islands; through Hāloa, the taro and the first man, all Hawaiians descend from him.

facets.facet_name: Earth Mother Who Gave Birth to Islands
facets.core_claim: Papa birthed the Hawaiian islands from her body; the land itself is her child and the people her descendants.

facets.facet_name: Shape-Shifting Pig God of Rain and Lover of Pele
facets.core_claim: Kamapuaʻa's rains and wild energy oppose and unite with Pele's fire; their struggle divides the islands into wet and dry.

facets.facet_name: Snow Goddess Who Contends with Pele
facets.core_claim: From Mauna Kea Poliʻahu answers Pele's fire with snow and cold, keeping balance on the island of Hawaiʻi.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Hula and Healing Who Revived the Dead
facets.core_claim: Hiʻiaka's chants heal and restore life; the hula is hers, and she cleared the islands of monsters on her great journey.

facets.facet_name: Shark God Who Guides Voyagers
facets.core_claim: Kamohoaliʻi leads lost canoes home and guards those who honor him; he is the greatest of shark ʻaumakua.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of Pulotu, Realm of the Dead
facets.core_claim: In Pulotu Hikuleʻo receives the spirits of the chiefs and rules the world beneath, as Tangaloa rules above and Maui on earth.

facets.facet_name: Eel-Bodied Lord of the Underworld
facets.core_claim: Saveasiʻuleo receives the spirits of the dead in Pulotu beneath the western sea.

facets.facet_name: War Goddess Who Distributed Sovereignty
facets.core_claim: Victorious Nafanua conferred the great titles of Samoa and prophesied a new kingdom from heaven.
facets.scholarly_note: Samoan Christians later read her prophecy as foretelling the arrival of the missionaries (1830).

facets.facet_name: Sky God Who Fathered the Sacred Kings
facets.core_claim: From the heavens Tangaloa descended to father the line of the Tuʻi Tonga and sent down the islands as wood-chips from his workbench.

facets.facet_name: Self-Created God Who Broke His Shell
facets.core_claim: Alone in the void Taʻaroa created himself, burst his shell and fashioned the cosmos from the shell and from his own body.

facets.facet_name: War God and Patron of the ʻArioi
facets.core_claim: ʻOro gives victory and receives sacrifice; through his son-like devotees, the ʻArioi, he also presides over festivity and the renewal of fertility.

facets.facet_name: Creator God of the Birdman Cult
facets.core_claim: Makemake made the first humans and brings the birds each spring; the Birdman contest at ʻOrongo is held in his honor.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Darkness and Lord of the Sea
facets.core_claim: Before all things was Tanaoa, darkness and the deep; light (Atea) and sound (Ono) emerged by overcoming him.

facets.facet_name: Light Who Became the Sky Father
facets.core_claim: Atea rose as light, drove Tanaoa's darkness away, and as Sky Father begot the gods and the Marquesan people.

facets.facet_name: The Very Beginning at the Root of the Cosmos
facets.core_claim: At the base of the cosmic coconut dwells Vari; from pieces of her own flesh she made the first gods and the world above her.

facets.facet_name: Sky God of Knowledge Who Came to Earth
facets.core_claim: Lugeilan, keeper of heavenly knowledge, descends from heaven to the world of humans; his son by a mortal woman is Olifat.
facets.scholarly_note: Names and genealogies differ across the Caroline Islands; Chuukese Luk is often treated as a cognate of Lugeilan.

facets.facet_name: Trickster Who Climbed to Heaven on Smoke
facets.core_claim: Olifat breaks every rule between heaven and earth: mischievous, cruel and generous, he gave the world fire and its dangers.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Brother Whose Body Became the World
facets.core_claim: Puntan gave his body to become the cosmos: sky, earth, sun, moon and rainbow are Puntan.

facets.facet_name: Sister Who Shaped the World and Birthed Humanity
facets.core_claim: Fuʻuna crafted the cosmos from Puntan and became the stone from which the Chamorro people emerged.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Creator in the Mountain Cave
facets.core_claim: From his cave Degei created humanity and sustains the world; his stirring causes earthquakes and thunder.

facets.facet_name: Judge of the Passing Souls
facets.core_claim: Every soul leaving Fiji passes Degei, who questions it and sends it to Murimuria or to punishment.

facets.facet_name: Shark God and Guardian of Fishermen
facets.core_claim: Dakuwaqa patrols the reefs; those under his protection, above all the people of Kadavu, are never harmed by sharks.

facets.facet_name: Spider Whose Buried Figures Brought Death
facets.core_claim: Copying Qat but burying his carvings, Marawa caused them to decay, and decay and death entered the world.

facets.facet_name: The Wise Culture-Hero Brother
facets.core_claim: To Kabinana fashions what is good and right in the world, and his wisdom sets the pattern for the Tolai.

facets.facet_name: The Foolish Brother Who Botched Creation
facets.core_claim: To Purgo's clumsy imitations produced the shark and the evils of the world, which his brother could not undo.

facets.facet_name: Sky Being of Initiation and Law
facets.core_claim: Daramulan established the initiation ceremonies and oversees the keeping of the law from the sky.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups. Only material published by 19th-century observers and later public sources is used; details of initiation are restricted and omitted.

facets.facet_name: Crow Ancestor and Bringer of Fire
facets.core_claim: Waa and Bunjil divide the Kulin world into two halves; Waa's cunning brought fire to everyone.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Ancestor Who Shaped the River and Went to the Sky
facets.core_claim: Ngurunderi's journey made the Murray, its lakes and the Coorong and laid down the law; he showed the way the spirits of the dead go to the sky.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Mouthless Beings of Rain and Law
facets.core_claim: The Wandjina bring the wet season and the renewal of life and enforce the law; their painted images are their living presence.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups. Each language group has its own named Wandjina (e.g. Namarali, Wodjin, Rimijmarra, already recorded).

facets.facet_name: Great Python Who Brings the Monsoon
facets.core_claim: Yurlunggur rises from his waterhole into the sky as the monsoon cloud and lightning, swallowing and restoring, making the seasons turn.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Sisters Whose Journey Named the Land
facets.core_claim: Walking and naming, the Sisters brought the country and its creatures into ordered being; their swallowing by the python is the turning of the year.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Creator Serpent of the Deep Pools
facets.core_claim: Ngalyod made the country and still lives in its waters, giving rain and life and punishing those who disturb sacred places.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Lightning Man Who Strikes with Stone Axes
facets.core_claim: Namarrkon's axes split the clouds; his storms bring the life-giving wet season and can strike down trees and people.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Whose Path Made the Rivers
facets.core_claim: The Waagal shaped the waterways of Noongar country and still dwells in them as their guardian.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Creators of Water and Rain
facets.core_claim: The serpent beings of the creation time made the waterways and live on in them, bringing rain and life and enforcing the law.
facets.scholarly_note: The single label "Rainbow Serpent" is an anthropological grouping; the beings it covers are distinct and Country-specific. Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Sleeping Ancestor from Whose Body Life Came
facets.core_claim: Karora dreamed in the earth and life came forth from his body; he rests still in the soak at Ilbalintja.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Father Who Decreed That All Must Die
facets.core_claim: Purukupali's grief made death final for all people and founded the pukumani ceremonies with their carved poles.
facets.scholarly_note: Drawn only from published, publicly available (non-restricted) material; restricted and secret-sacred knowledge is deliberately excluded. Authority over these narratives rests with the custodians of the relevant Country, and versions differ between language groups.

facets.facet_name: Bringer of Malo's Law
facets.core_claim: Malo-Bomai gave the Meriam their law: Malo keeps his hands to himself and does not take what belongs to another.
facets.scholarly_note: Only published, non-restricted material is used; the inner Malo-Bomai ceremonies are restricted.

facets.facet_name: King of Ghosts and Queller of Demons
facets.core_claim: Zhong Kui, the scholar denied the first rank for his ugliness who took his own life, was made king of ghosts by the emperor of heaven; his fierce painted image on the door drives demons away.

facets.facet_name: Kitchen God Who Reports to Heaven
facets.core_claim: From the stove Zao Jun watches the household all year; on the 23rd or 24th of the twelfth month he ascends to report its deeds to the Jade Emperor, and his lips are sweetened with malt candy.

facets.facet_name: Duke of Thunder Who Punishes Hidden Crimes
facets.core_claim: With drum, mallet and chisel the bird-faced Lei Gong strikes down those guilty of secret crimes, especially the unfilial and those who waste grain.

facets.facet_name: Mother of Lightning with Her Mirrors
facets.core_claim: Dian Mu flashes her two mirrors to light up the guilty so that Lei Gong's thunderbolt strikes true.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Soil and Locality
facets.core_claim: Every street, field and village has its Tudigong, the lowest official of the celestial bureaucracy, who guards the place, blesses its harvest and reports to the City God.

facets.facet_name: Thunder Kami Beating the Drums
facets.core_claim: Raijin beats his ring of drums to make thunder and brings the storms and rain on which the rice depends.

facets.facet_name: Wind Kami with the Bag of Winds
facets.core_claim: Fūjin carries the winds in a great bag over his shoulders and releases them across the world.

facets.facet_name: Dragon King of the Sea Palace
facets.core_claim: Ryūjin rules the palace Ryūgū-jō beneath the sea and controls the tides with his jewels of ebb and flow.

facets.facet_name: Mireuk the Creator Cheated of His World (Changse-ga)
facets.core_claim: In the shaman song of creation Mireuk separated heaven and earth and made the first people, but Seokga stole the world from him by cheating in a flower-growing contest; that is why the world is full of thieves and evil.
facets.scholarly_note: From the Changse-ga creation muga recorded in Hamhung in 1923.

facets.facet_name: Mireuk, the Coming Buddha (Korean Maitreya)
facets.core_claim: Mireuk, the future Buddha, will come to establish a world of peace; Koreans carved great Mireuk statues in stone and awaited him in messianic movements.

facets.facet_name: Atua of Cultivated Food and Peace
facets.core_claim: Rongo, son of Rangi and Papa, governs the kūmara and all cultivated food and the peace in which gardens can grow.

facets.facet_name: Hina Who Went to the Moon
facets.core_claim: Weary of endless labor, Hina left the earth for the moon, where she can still be seen beating tapa cloth.

facets.facet_name: Tagaloa-a-Lagi, Creator Above the Heavens
facets.core_claim: Tagaloa-a-Lagi existed alone in the void above the heavens; he made the rocks, the earth and the sea, and sent his daughter, the plover Tuli, to find dry land, from which the islands and people came.

facets.facet_name: Tagaro, Creator and Wise Brother
facets.core_claim: In northern Vanuatu Tagaro made the land, people and good things, while his foolish brother Suqe spoiled them and brought death and hardship.
facets.scholarly_note: Recorded for Maewo and neighboring islands in R. H. Codrington, The Melanesians (1891); the Tagaro–Tangaroa connection is debated.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Moon and the Months
facets.core_claim: Nanna is the radiant crescent who orders the months; at his new-moon rising the cattle multiply and the land is fed.

facets.facet_name: Father of the Sun and the Evening Star
facets.core_claim: From Nanna come Utu the Sun and Inanna the Evening Star: the lights of heaven descend from the Moon.

facets.facet_name: The Bridegroom Taken to the Netherworld
facets.core_claim: Dumuzi goes down to the land of no return in Inanna's place and comes up again for half the year; his descent is the withering of the pasture and his return its greening.

facets.facet_name: Shepherd-King of the Sacred Marriage
facets.core_claim: As Inanna's chosen husband Dumuzi is the model of the king who weds the goddess so that the land prospers.

facets.facet_name: Queen Beside Enlil
facets.core_claim: Ninlil shares Enlil's throne and with him decrees destinies; her children are the Moon and the lords of the underworld.

facets.facet_name: Serpent Gatekeeper Between Heaven and the Netherworld
facets.core_claim: Ningishzida coils between the realms: he stands at Anu's gate with Dumuzi, and below he keeps the roots and the throne of the dead.

facets.facet_name: The Mother Who Bore Heaven and Earth
facets.core_claim: Before An and Ki were separated there was Nammu, the waters without beginning, and from her all gods were born.

facets.facet_name: Initiator of Humanity's Creation
facets.core_claim: Nammu wakes Enki from sleep and sets him to fashion humankind from the clay of the Abzu.

facets.facet_name: Champion of Enlil, Slayer of Anzu and Asag
facets.core_claim: Ninurta, son of Enlil, defeats Asag and the stone warriors of the mountains, recovers the Tablet of Destinies from Anzu, and turns the conquered stones into dykes that water the fields.

facets.facet_name: Sumerian Storm and Rain Lord
facets.core_claim: Ishkur rides the storm and brings rain to the uplands or withholds it; he is the roaring lion-dragon of the clouds.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Harran, King of the Gods (Nabonidus)
facets.core_claim: Sîn is lord of the crown of heaven; the gods tremble before him, and the king who honours him is given dominion.

facets.facet_name: Holder of the Tablet of Destinies for Tiamat
facets.core_claim: Kingu was raised by Tiamat to supreme command and wore the Tablet of Destinies that belongs only to the rightful king of the gods.

facets.facet_name: The God Whose Blood Became Humanity
facets.core_claim: Humankind is made from the blood of the slain rebel god, so that people carry divine substance and the burden of service.

facets.facet_name: Queen of Heaven, Consort of the Storm King
facets.core_claim: Hebat leads the procession of goddesses to meet Teshub; she is mother of Sharruma and queen of all the gods.

facets.facet_name: Storm God of Hatti, King of Heaven
facets.core_claim: Tarhunz is the conqueror: he thunders from the mountains, brings rain to the fields, and the Great King rules Hatti as his steward.

facets.facet_name: Sun Goddess, Queen of the Land of Hatti
facets.core_claim: The Sun Goddess of Arinna holds the kingship of Hatti and entrusts it to the Great King; she is the light that judges and protects the land.

facets.facet_name: The God Who Vanished and Returned
facets.core_claim: When Telipinu turns away in anger, all growth stops in heaven and earth; when he is found and soothed, abundance returns and the eya-tree is hung with plenty.

facets.facet_name: First King in Heaven
facets.core_claim: Alalu sat on the throne of heaven in the earliest days; Anu, who bowed at his feet, deposed him and he went below.

facets.facet_name: The Stone Giant Who Rose Against Heaven
facets.core_claim: Ullikummi, deaf and blind stone, grows to threaten the gods' city until his feet are severed from the bearer of the world.

facets.facet_name: The Serpent Who Overcame the Storm God
facets.core_claim: Illuyanka once beat the Storm God and held his strength, until he was tricked, bound and slain so that the land could flourish.

facets.facet_name: Hurrian Goddess of Love and War
facets.core_claim: Shaushka moves between battle and desire, between the gods and the goddesses; she charms monsters and grants victory to her favourites.

facets.facet_name: Ruler of the Dark Earth
facets.core_claim: Lelwani keeps the dark earth where the dead go down; the king's life may be ransomed by gifts to her house.

facets.facet_name: Judge of the Dead at Susa
facets.core_claim: Inshushinak sits in judgment over the souls brought before him and assigns each its fate in the world below.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Susa and Guardian of Oaths
facets.core_claim: The kings of Elam rule as servants of Inshushinak, lord of Susa, and swear by his name.

facets.facet_name: Great God of Elam
facets.core_claim: Humban is the great one who extends his protection over the king and the land of Elam.
facets.scholarly_note: Whether Napirisha ('great god') is an epithet of Humban or a separate deity is debated; this record follows the identification only as a possibility.

facets.facet_name: Great Goddess and Mother of the Gods
facets.core_claim: Kiririsha is the great lady and mother of the gods, worshipped beside the great god in his ziggurat.

facets.facet_name: Supreme God of Urartu
facets.core_claim: Haldi goes before the army; through him the king conquers, and to him the first share of every victory is given.

facets.facet_name: Storm and War God of Urartu
facets.core_claim: Teisheba thunders over the highlands and fights beside Haldi for the king of Urartu.

facets.facet_name: Sun God of Urartu
facets.core_claim: Shivini is the sun that sees all the land, third of the great gods of Urartu.

facets.facet_name: Lady of Love and Battle
facets.core_claim: Astarte is the bright goddess of desire and of the hunt and battle; Sidon is her city and its kings her priests.

facets.facet_name: The Evening Star
facets.core_claim: Astarte is the planet that rises at dusk, the heavenly lady of the West Semitic world.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Healing at Sidon
facets.core_claim: Eshmun heals at the sacred spring; the sick bathe in his waters and give thanks with images of the children he restored.

facets.facet_name: The Youth Restored to Life
facets.core_claim: Eshmun died young and was made divine by the goddess who loved him.
facets.scholarly_note: The castration-and-revival story is known only from the late Neoplatonist Damascius.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Carthage and the Harvest
facets.core_claim: Baal Hammon is the old king of the gods of Carthage, who gives the harvest and receives the vows of the city.
facets.scholarly_note: The meaning of the tophet offerings (child sacrifice versus burial of infants) remains debated.

facets.facet_name: The Archer of Plague
facets.core_claim: Resheph shoots arrows of pestilence and stands guard at the gate of the dead; yet he who sends the plague can also turn it away.

facets.facet_name: Divine Smith and Builder
facets.core_claim: Kothar forges the weapons of victory and raises the house of the king of the gods; his skill is a kind of wisdom and spell.

facets.facet_name: Torch of the Gods Who Passes Through the Underworld
facets.core_claim: Shapash crosses into the land of the dead each night; she carries the fallen and brings word between the living gods and those below.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Offering Through Fire
facets.core_claim: To Molek, king of the dead, the firstborn were given at the Tophet; the prophets of Yahweh named this the greatest abomination.
facets.scholarly_note: Since Otto Eissfeldt (1935) many scholars read molk as a sacrifice term rather than a god's name; others accept a deity Malik/Milku. Biblical sources are hostile.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Grain and Father of Baal
facets.core_claim: Dagan is the grain-lord of the Middle Euphrates and of the Philistine coast, father of Baal and giver of the harvest.
facets.scholarly_note: The medieval derivation of the name from Hebrew dag 'fish' is folk etymology; Dagan is a grain god (Ugaritic dgn 'grain').

facets.facet_name: National God of Moab
facets.core_claim: Chemosh is lord of Moab: his anger brings defeat, his favour brings victory, and captured cities are devoted to him.

facets.facet_name: King-God of Ammon
facets.core_claim: Milcom is the king of the Ammonites who wears the great crown of Rabbah.

facets.facet_name: The Syrian Goddess of Hierapolis
facets.core_claim: Atargatis sits enthroned between lions as mother of the city; her sacred fish and doves are never harmed.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Heaven
facets.core_claim: Baalshamin is master of the heavens, who gives rain and answers kings who lift their hands to him.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Kaaba's Divining Arrows
facets.core_claim: Hubal stood within the House at Mecca; the Quraysh cast the arrows before him, and his answer settled what they should do.

facets.facet_name: The Goddess of Ta'if
facets.core_claim: Allat is the goddess, guardian of her sanctuary and of those who take refuge there; her stone at Ta'if was clothed and honoured.

facets.facet_name: One of the Three Daughters
facets.core_claim: With al-Uzza and Manat she was called upon as an intercessor whose favour is hoped for.
facets.scholarly_note: The Quran (53:19–23) rejects the claim that these are daughters of God.

facets.facet_name: The Mightiest, Goddess of the Morning Star
facets.core_claim: Al-Uzza, the Mighty, dwells in the three acacias of Nakhla; the Quraysh made their circuit for her and called her in battle.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Fate and Portion
facets.core_claim: Manat measures each person's share and the hour of their death; pilgrims shaved their heads at her shrine.

facets.facet_name: God of Love and Friendship
facets.core_claim: Wadd is love and amity; 'Wadd is father' said the Minaeans, and they placed their land under his protection.
facets.scholarly_note: Wadd's lunar character is often asserted but rests on the serpent-and-crescent iconography; it is not certain.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Mountains, God of the King
facets.core_claim: Dushara is lord of the Shara; his throne is the stone, and the Nabataean kings ruled as his people.

facets.facet_name: National God of Saba
facets.core_claim: Almaqah is lord of Saba; the dam and the fields are his, and the people of Saba are his children.

facets.facet_name: The Morning Star, First of the Gods
facets.core_claim: ʿAthtar is invoked first of the gods; he waters the fields and his star rises in the east.

facets.facet_name: The Star Who Could Not Fill Baal's Throne
facets.core_claim: When Baal died, ʿAthtar the Terrible was set on the throne of Zaphon; his feet did not reach the stool, and he came down to rule the earth.

facets.facet_name: The Immaculate Heavenly River
facets.core_claim: Aredvi Sura Anahita pours down from the heights as all the waters of the world, cleansing seed and womb and giving milk to mothers.

facets.facet_name: Granter of Victory to Kings
facets.core_claim: Heroes from Yima to Vishtaspa offered to Anahita, and she gave them victory over their enemies.

facets.facet_name: Guardian of the Covenant
facets.core_claim: Mithra is the contract itself: he watches every agreement and destroys the house and lands of the Mithra-deceiver.

facets.facet_name: Herald of the Sun and Judge of Souls
facets.core_claim: Mithra rides out before the immortal swift-horsed Sun and stands at the Bridge where souls are judged.

facets.facet_name: Good Mind, First of the Amesha Spentas
facets.core_claim: Vohu Manah, the Good Mind, is the first creation of Ahura Mazda; he welcomed Zarathustra to the presence of the Wise Lord and receives the righteous soul in paradise. Cattle are his creation.

facets.facet_name: Best Truth, Guardian of Fire
facets.core_claim: Asha Vahishta is the order of the world made holy; every fire tended and every truth spoken is his.

facets.facet_name: Holy Devotion, the Earth Herself
facets.core_claim: Spenta Armaiti is the earth and humble devotion together; she bears all creatures and is gladdened by the ploughman.

facets.facet_name: Desirable Dominion
facets.core_claim: Khshathra Vairya is the rule of the good that will come in fullness; metal and the strength to protect the poor are his.

facets.facet_name: Wholeness and Immortality
facets.core_claim: Haurvatat gives health and the waters; Ameretat gives deathlessness and the plants; together they are the reward of the righteous.

facets.facet_name: Smiter of Resistance, Giver of Victory
facets.core_claim: Verethragna, best-armed of the yazatas, breaks the resistance of enemies and comes to the faithful in ten forms.

facets.facet_name: The Three-Headed Dragon of the Lie
facets.core_claim: Azhi Dahaka, full of a thousand sorceries, was made by the Evil Spirit to empty the world of the righteous; bound under Damavand, he will be loosed and slain at the renovation.

facets.facet_name: King of the Golden Age and the Var
facets.core_claim: Yima ruled a thousand years without death; when the winters came he built the var and sheltered the seed of every good creature.

facets.facet_name: The Primal Man Whose Death Seeded Humanity
facets.core_claim: Gayomart died at the onset of evil, and from his body the metals and from his seed humankind came forth.

facets.facet_name: King of the Realm of Light
facets.core_claim: The Father of Greatness is light without limit, the one root of all good; nothing evil can touch his kingdom.

facets.facet_name: The Ruler of Darkness Who Invaded the Light
facets.core_claim: The Prince of Darkness is eternal evil and desire; he rose against the Light, devoured its particles, and binds them in matter until the end.

facets.facet_name: Builder of the Cosmos from the Bodies of Archons
facets.core_claim: The Living Spirit fashions the world as a great machine for refining the captive light back to its source.

facets.facet_name: Pilot of the Ships of Light
facets.core_claim: The Messenger shows his beauty to the powers of darkness and draws the stolen light up through the moon and sun to the Father.

facets.facet_name: The Primal Man Who Gave Himself to the Darkness
facets.core_claim: Called forth by the Mother of Life, the Primal Man armed himself with his five sons, the light-elements, and let them be swallowed by Darkness as bait; rescued by the Living Spirit, he left his armour behind as the light scattered in the world.

facets.facet_name: Apostle of Light and Seal of the Prophets
facets.core_claim: Mani, visited by his heavenly Twin, is the last apostle after Zoroaster, the Buddha and Jesus, who brought the complete revelation of the two principles and the three times.

facets.facet_name: The Sole God, Creator of All
facets.core_claim: O sole god, like whom there is no other! You made the earth as you wished, you alone; when you rise all live, when you set they die.

facets.facet_name: The Disc Whose Rays Give Life
facets.core_claim: The Aten's rays reach down as hands to the king, his only son who knows him, and through the king life passes to the land.

facets.facet_name: The Limitless Primeval Waters
facets.core_claim: Before heaven and earth, before the gods, there was Nun, inert and boundless; all things came out of him and all are still encircled by him.

facets.facet_name: Creator from the Primeval Waters
facets.core_claim: Neith emerged from Nun, spoke the world into being in seven words and gave birth to Ra; she is the self-generated mother.

facets.facet_name: Archer and Opener of Ways
facets.core_claim: Neith's crossed arrows guard the king and the dead.

facets.facet_name: The Air That Holds Heaven Apart
facets.core_claim: Shu stands between Geb and Nut and lifts the sky; in him all breathe, and he is the life that Atum breathed out.

facets.facet_name: Moisture and the Distant Eye
facets.core_claim: Tefnut is the dew and the order of moisture; when she departs as the raging lioness, the land dries, and when she returns it is renewed.

facets.facet_name: Guardian of Birth and the Home
facets.core_claim: Bes watches over women in childbirth and over sleeping children; his grimace and his dancing drive off every evil.

facets.facet_name: The Living Bull, Herald of Ptah
facets.core_claim: Apis is Ptah's living image on earth; at his death he goes to Osiris, and a new Apis is born.

facets.facet_name: Devourer of the Unjust Heart
facets.core_claim: Ammit crouches by the balance: the heart that fails the weighing is hers, and its owner ceases to exist.

facets.facet_name: The Self-Created Lord of Totality
facets.core_claim: Atum, the Complete One, came into being by himself on the primeval mound out of Nun and generated Shu and Tefnut from his own substance; at the end of time he alone will remain with Osiris.

facets.facet_name: Protective Cat and Gentle Eye of Ra
facets.core_claim: Bastet of Bubastis guards home and mother; she is the lioness pacified into the cat, the gentle Eye of Ra.

facets.facet_name: The Primordial Chasm
facets.core_claim: Before Earth, before Eros, there was the yawning gap; all darkness and all light descend from it.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Night, Mother of Powers
facets.core_claim: Black Night, born of Chaos, bore Day and Aether, and alone bore Death, Sleep, Dreams, the Fates and Nemesis; even Zeus fears to displease her.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Darkness Under the Earth
facets.core_claim: Erebus is the deep darkness that existed from the first and lies beneath the earth on the road of the dead.

facets.facet_name: The Abyss-Prison of the Defeated Gods
facets.core_claim: Tartarus is the bottom of the world: a bronze anvil would fall nine days to reach it, and there the overthrown powers are bound.

facets.facet_name: Divine Law and Right Order
facets.core_claim: Themis is what is fitting by divine ordinance; she sits beside Zeus and calls the gods to assembly.

facets.facet_name: The First Sky, Overthrown by His Son
facets.core_claim: Ouranos covered Gaia and would not let their children be born; Kronos castrated him with the adamant sickle, and from his blood came the Erinyes and from the foam Aphrodite.

facets.facet_name: Primordial Desire That Joins All Things
facets.core_claim: Eros, fairest of the deathless gods, came into being with Earth at the beginning; he loosens limbs and makes all generation possible.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Wild, Flocks and Panic
facets.core_claim: Goat-footed Pan roams the Arcadian heights, piping on the syrinx; he guards shepherds and sends sudden panic on those who intrude.

facets.facet_name: Death, Twin of Sleep
facets.core_claim: Thanatos, son of Night, comes to mortals at their hour; iron-hearted, he takes them gently to the house of Hades.

facets.facet_name: The First-Born Who Brings All to Light
facets.core_claim: Phanes leapt from the silver egg and lit up the dark; he holds the seeds of the gods, and from him the world is made manifest.

facets.facet_name: Swallowed by Zeus, Reborn as the Cosmos
facets.core_claim: When Zeus swallowed Phanes, all things were made new within Zeus: the first-born lives on as the inside of the world.

facets.facet_name: Ageless Time, Layer of the Cosmic Egg
facets.core_claim: Before all gods was unaging Chronos, coiled with Necessity around the world; from him came the egg of all things.
facets.scholarly_note: Distinct from the Titan Kronos, though ancient writers often played on the two names.

facets.facet_name: Queen of the Gods, Protectress of the City
facets.core_claim: Uni is the great queen beside Tinia; she gives kingship and suckles the hero who becomes divine.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Wisdom, War and Crafts
facets.core_claim: Menrva springs armed from the head of Tinia; she counsels heroes and hurls one of the thunderbolts.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Love and Life
facets.core_claim: Turan is the lady of desire, winged and adorned, who unites lovers and gives life its bloom.

facets.facet_name: Messenger and Guide of Souls
facets.core_claim: Turms carries the word of the gods and leads souls down to Aita's house.

facets.facet_name: Winged Guide of the Dead
facets.core_claim: Vanth is present at the moment of death; she lights the dead one's road with her torch and keeps the record of their fate.

facets.facet_name: God of Wine and Growth
facets.core_claim: Fufluns is the rising sap and the vine; with him come feast and revel.

facets.facet_name: Youthful God of War
facets.core_claim: Laran is the young warrior in helmet and cuirass, spear in hand.

facets.facet_name: King of the Dead
facets.core_claim: Aita rules the house of the dead with Phersipnai; the wolf's head is his crown.

facets.facet_name: Revealer of the Etruscan Discipline
facets.core_claim: Tages sprang from the earth and taught the twelve lords of Etruria how to read the will of the gods; all haruspicy is his gift.

facets.facet_name: Woodland God and Oracle of Dreams
facets.core_claim: Faunus protects the herds and fields and speaks in dreams to those who sleep on the fleeces of sacrifice in his grove.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of War and Its Declaration
facets.core_claim: Bellona drives the chariot of battle; war is not begun until the spear is cast from her column.

facets.facet_name: Fortune Who Steers and Gives
facets.core_claim: Fortuna guides every life with her rudder and pours plenty from her horn; her wheel lifts and casts down.

facets.facet_name: Punisher of Broken Oaths, Taker of the Dead
facets.core_claim: Orcus seizes those whose time has come and punishes the oath-breaker in the world below.

facets.facet_name: Quirinus, the Deified Romulus
facets.core_claim: Quirinus is the god of the Roman people in assembly, the Quirites; Romulus was taken up into heaven and revealed himself as Quirinus.
facets.scholarly_note: Dumézil placed Quirinus as the third-function member of the archaic Jupiter–Mars–Quirinus triad; this is contested.

facets.facet_name: The Boundary Stone
facets.core_claim: Terminus is the stone that marks the field; when Jupiter's temple was built on the Capitol, Terminus alone would not move, and so the boundary of Rome would never retreat.

facets.facet_name: King of the Golden Age
facets.core_claim: Saturn, fleeing Jupiter, hid in Latium and taught its people to farm; his reign was the Golden Age, recalled each Saturnalia when masters served slaves.

facets.facet_name: Teacher of Immortality Who Returned from Hiding
facets.core_claim: Zalmoxis promised the Getae that they do not die but go to him; he vanished below the earth and came back in the fourth year.

facets.facet_name: Thracian Huntress and Moon
facets.core_claim: Bendis hunts with two spears in the forests of Thrace and rides the night with torches.

facets.facet_name: Sky-Father of the Mysteries
facets.core_claim: Sabazios is the lord of heaven who comes to his initiates as a serpent; his raised hand blesses and protects.

facets.facet_name: The Divine Rider at the Serpent Tree
facets.core_claim: Heros rides out from the sacred tree to protect, to heal and to carry the heroised dead.

facets.facet_name: Rider-Protector of Risinium
facets.core_claim: Medaurus rides high above Risinium with his lance, guarding the city and those who come from it.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Sacred Spring
facets.core_claim: Bindus is the spirit of the spring that rises from the rock; the Iapodes' chieftains set their altars at his waters.

facets.facet_name: Healer and Dream-Oracle
facets.core_claim: Endovelicus answers those who sleep in his sanctuary, healing them and granting what they vow for.
facets.scholarly_note: His chthonic character is inferred from boar iconography and dream-oracle practice.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Rebirth and Avenging Justice
facets.core_claim: Ataegina brings the spring back from below and avenges wrongs brought to her in writing.

facets.facet_name: Guardian of the Community
facets.core_claim: Bandua binds a people together and defends them; each town calls him by its own name.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Springs and Valleys
facets.core_claim: Nabia lives in the spring and the river valley; to her the waters and the herds that drink them belong.

facets.facet_name: The Giving God, the Sun
facets.core_claim: Dazhbog is the sun, son of Svarog, the god who gives; the people of Rus' are called his grandchildren.

facets.facet_name: Celestial Smith and Father of the Sun
facets.core_claim: Svarog, whom the chronicler called Hephaestus, forged the first tongs from heaven, established marriage and law, and fathered the sun Dazhbog.

facets.facet_name: Winter and Death, Drowned at Spring
facets.core_claim: Morana is the death of the year: her straw image is carried out of the village, burned or drowned, so that spring may enter.

facets.facet_name: The Black God of Misfortune
facets.core_claim: Chernobog is the evil god; at the feast the cup is passed and his name spoken over it, for all ill fortune is in his power.

facets.facet_name: The White God of Good Fortune
facets.core_claim: Belobog gives all good things, as Chernobog sends the bad; the bright and the black divide the world between them.
facets.scholarly_note: No medieval source names Belobog; he is a modern inference from Helmold's statement that the Slavs believed in a good god opposed to the black god.

facets.facet_name: Grandfather of the Winds
facets.core_claim: The winds are Stribog's grandchildren; they rush from the sea and drive arrows into the ranks of warriors.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Kin, Birth and Destiny
facets.core_claim: Rod and the Rozhanitsy stand at every birth and give the child its fate; to them the table is laid at the feast of kin.
facets.scholarly_note: Modern reconstructions making Rod the supreme creator of the Slavs go beyond the sermons, which list him with lesser powers.

facets.facet_name: Four-Faced Lord of Arkona
facets.core_claim: Svantevit looks to all four quarters; his horn tells the harvest, his horse tells the war, and all the Rani bring him tribute.

facets.facet_name: Blossoming Earth Mother
facets.core_claim: Žemyna, the flowerer, feeds all that lives and takes back the dead; she is honoured first at the table.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Dead, Foe of the Thunderer
facets.core_claim: Velnias hides in trees, stones and animals; wherever he hides Perkūnas strikes, and the dead are his flock.

facets.facet_name: The Unfaithful Moon Husband
facets.core_claim: Mėnulis wedded the Sun and then courted the Morning Star; Perkūnas cut him with his sword, and so he wanes.

facets.facet_name: Virgin of the Air Whose Knee Bore the World
facets.core_claim: Ilmatar lay on the waters until the egg broke on her knee and became heaven and earth; with her hands she shaped the headlands and the deeps.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Tuonela
facets.core_claim: Tuoni's realm lies across the black river; whoever drinks Tuonetar's beer does not return.

facets.facet_name: King of the Waters and the Catch
facets.core_claim: Ahti rules the waters from his dwelling under the waves and gives fish to those who honour him.

facets.facet_name: King of the Forest and Its Game
facets.core_claim: Tapio holds the beasts of the forest; when the hunter sings well, he opens his golden storehouse.

facets.facet_name: The Hero Torn Apart and Restored by His Mother
facets.core_claim: Lemminkäinen was hewn to pieces in Tuoni's river; his mother gathered every piece and called him back to life.

facets.facet_name: Smith of the Sky-Vault and the Sampo
facets.core_claim: Ilmarinen forged the lid of heaven and the Sampo that grinds out grain, salt and gold.

facets.facet_name: Spirit of the Sacred Grove Turned Demon
facets.core_claim: Hiisi dwells in the dark woods and rocky hills; his creatures are the wasp, the snake and the disease-arrow.

facets.facet_name: Thunderer with Two Hammers
facets.core_claim: Horagalles strikes the trolls with his hammers and guards people and reindeer from the powers that harm them.

facets.facet_name: The Ruling Father
facets.core_claim: Ráđđeáhčči is the highest; he creates the souls and sends them down, while his son does his work in the world.
facets.scholarly_note: Some scholars suspect Christian Trinitarian influence on the missionary-reported Radien family.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of Birth Under the Hearth
facets.core_claim: Sáráhkká forms the body of the child and opens the way at birth; she shares the mother's pain.

facets.facet_name: Bow Woman, Guardian of Children
facets.core_claim: Juksáhkká holds the bow; she shapes the unborn and guards little children as they learn to walk.

facets.facet_name: Door Woman, Guardian of the Threshold
facets.core_claim: Uksáhkká dwells beneath the doorway and keeps watch over all who pass and over the child at birth.

facets.facet_name: Old Woman of the Realm of the Dead
facets.core_claim: Jábmeáhkká receives the dead below; the noaidi bargains with her for the souls of the sick.

facets.facet_name: Great God of the Oeselians
facets.core_claim: Tharapita was born on the forest hill and flew to Ösel; there his people honoured him in the sacred grove.

facets.facet_name: The Old Heathen Outwitted by the Farmhand
facets.core_claim: Vanapagan owns great wealth and strength, but Kaval-Ants always tricks him out of it.

facets.facet_name: The Adversary Who Dove for the Earth
facets.core_claim: Ördög fetched the sand from which Isten made the earth, but kept some for himself, and so the world has rough mountains and his mischief.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the Forest and Keeper of the First Arts
facets.core_claim: Basajaun protects the flocks and owned the wheat and the arts of the forge; humans won them by cunning.

facets.facet_name: Grandmother Sun
facets.core_claim: Eguzki, grandmother sun, drives off the beings of the night and goes home to her mother the Earth at evening.

facets.facet_name: Chief God of Kartli
facets.core_claim: Armazi stands on the mountain above the royal city; the king and his people bow to him as lord of the land.

facets.facet_name: Patron of Men, Warriors and Travellers
facets.core_claim: Uastyrdzhi rides out to help travellers and warriors who call on him, and punishes the oath-breaker and the thief.

facets.facet_name: The Steel-Bodied Hero Who Fought Heaven
facets.core_claim: Batradz is the steel Nart; no blade can harm him, and he avenged his kin on the very spirits of heaven.

facets.facet_name: The Hero Whose Sword Is Returned to the Sea
facets.core_claim: Batradz would not die until his sword was cast into the sea; then the waters boiled and he could rest.

facets.facet_name: Thunder-Lord of the Harvest
facets.core_claim: Uatsilla brings rain to the wheat and fire to the wrongdoer; one struck by his lightning is holy.

facets.facet_name: Ruler and Judge of the Dead
facets.core_claim: Barastyr sits at the entrance of the land of the dead and sends each soul to its place.

facets.facet_name: The Heavenly Smith
facets.core_claim: Kurdalægon's forge stands in heaven; he hardens heroes like steel and makes the arms of the Narts.

facets.facet_name: The Great God Above All
facets.core_claim: Thashxo is the creator who rules all; the other powers act by his will, and Habze is the way he has given.

facets.facet_name: Lord of Thunder and Lightning
facets.core_claim: Shible strikes with the lightning; whom he touches is his own, mourned with dancing rather than tears.

facets.facet_name: Smith of the Narts
facets.core_claim: Tlepsh forged the tongs with his own hands and gave the Narts iron, the plough-share and the sickle.

facets.facet_name: Dragon-Reaper Born of Fire
facets.core_claim: Vahagn, born from the burning reed, wars against the vishaps and frees the waters and the land.

facets.facet_name: Straw-Thief Who Made the Milky Way
facets.core_claim: Vahagn carried off straw in winter, and the trail he scattered became the Straw-Thief's Way across the sky.

facets.facet_name: Little Star, Goddess of Love and Water
facets.core_claim: Astghik is the beloved of Vahagn; her festival scatters roses and water over the land.

facets.facet_name: Scribe of the Supreme God
facets.core_claim: Tir writes down what Aramazd decrees and reveals it to mortals in dreams.

facets.facet_name: The Earth and the World Beneath
facets.core_claim: Spandaramet is the earth that feeds the vine and receives the dead into its depths.

facets.facet_name: Sky-God of the Albanians
facets.core_claim: Perëndi is heaven above, who sends the thunder and to whom oaths are sworn.
facets.scholarly_note: The etymology (often *per- 'strike' + ndi 'sky/day', or from Latin imperator) is disputed.

facets.facet_name: God of the Hearth-Fire
facets.core_claim: Enji is the fire of the house; it is fed, respected and sworn by.
facets.scholarly_note: Reconstructed largely from the weekday name; a full cult is not documented.

facets.facet_name: Winged Storm-Hero Against the Dragon
facets.core_claim: The drangue rises into the storm to strike the kulshedra so that the rain may fall and the springs flow.

facets.facet_name: Dragon Who Withholds the Waters
facets.core_claim: Kulshedra hoards the springs and burns the land; only the drangue's lightning can defeat her.

facets.facet_name: Inventor of All the Arts
facets.core_claim: Lugus is the master of every skill and every road; the Gauls honour him above all and many images of him stand among them.

facets.facet_name: The Woodcutter Lord
facets.core_claim: Esus cuts the sacred tree; offerings to him hang in the branches.

facets.facet_name: The Bright Healer
facets.core_claim: Belenus shines and heals; Aquileia trusted him to defend its walls.

facets.facet_name: Binder by Eloquence
facets.core_claim: Ogmios draws men after him by the chains of his speech; his strength is the word.

facets.facet_name: The Great Provider
facets.core_claim: Rosmerta holds the cornucopia and the purse; with Mercury she brings plenty.

facets.facet_name: The Thunderer with the Wheel
facets.core_claim: Taranis is the thunder; his wheel rolls across the sky, and Lucan names his altar as no less cruel than Scythian Diana's.

facets.facet_name: God of the Tribe
facets.core_claim: Teutates is the god of the people (teuta); the Berne scholiast says victims were drowned head-first in a vat for him.

facets.facet_name: The Spear-Struck God Restored from the Oak
facets.core_claim: Lleu could die only in an impossible place and way; slain, he became an eagle on the oak, and was sung back into his body.

facets.facet_name: Lleu of the Skilful Hand
facets.core_claim: With one cast he struck the wren between sinew and bone, and was named the Bright One of the Skilful Hand.

facets.facet_name: The Venerable Head Guarding Britain
facets.core_claim: Brân's head kept company with his men in an otherworld feast and lay under the White Mount as the shield of the island.

facets.facet_name: Giant King and Giver of the Cauldron of Rebirth
facets.core_claim: Brân gave the cauldron that restores the dead to life, though they rise without speech.

facets.facet_name: The Divine Youth Stolen and Freed
facets.core_claim: Mabon was taken from between his mother and the wall; only the oldest of creatures knew where, and his release was the key to the great hunt.

facets.facet_name: The Divine Mother
facets.core_claim: Modron is the mother whose son was taken; through her the divine child returns.

facets.facet_name: Lady of the Silver Wheel Who Shapes Her Son's Destiny
facets.core_claim: Arianrhod, stepping over Math's wand, bore two sons; she swore fates upon Lleu that only Gwydion's cunning could undo.

facets.facet_name: Lady of the Hot Spring and Justice
facets.core_claim: Sulis heals in the steaming waters and avenges the wronged who write to her in lead.

facets.facet_name: Healer and Catcher at the Severn
facets.core_claim: Nodens heals those who sleep in his temple and recovers what is stolen.

facets.facet_name: The Sun Goddess, Healer and Charioteer
facets.core_claim: Sunna rides the sky and was called with the gods to charm Balder's horse whole again.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of the Marsi Festival
facets.core_claim: Tamfana's temple was the most famous among the tribes; to her the Marsi held their great feast.

facets.facet_name: Goddess of the Battle Grove
facets.core_claim: In Baduhenna's grove the Frisians destroyed the invaders.

facets.facet_name: Typhon, the Monster Who Unmanned Zeus
facets.core_claim: Typhon, last child of Gaia and Tartarus, cut the sinews from Zeus's hands and feet and hid them in the Corycian cave, until Hermes stole them back and Zeus buried the monster under Etna.

facets.facet_name: Fortune of Cities and Persons
facets.core_claim: Tyche turns the fortunes of every city and person; with the cornucopia and the rudder she gives and steers.

facets.facet_name: Owner of the sacred leaves
facets.core_claim: Osanyin alone knows the secret virtue of every leaf; the other orisha received their portions of herbal power only when Shango's wife Oya scattered his calabash with the wind.

facets.facet_name: Hunter whose arrow never misses
facets.core_claim: Ochosi fires one arrow and it always finds its target; he hunts the prey that feeds the community and pursues the wrongdoer so that justice is done.

facets.facet_name: The ancestors who return in masquerade
facets.core_claim: The dead do not vanish; the Egungun come back through the masked dancer, whose body no one may touch, to judge, bless and protect the lineage.

facets.facet_name: Owner of the abyssal sea
facets.core_claim: Olokun rules the bottom of the ocean where no light reaches; all the wealth of the sea is Olokun's, and Olokun's anger is the flood.

facets.facet_name: The sacred twins
facets.core_claim: Twins are a single soul in two bodies and bring wealth and blessing to those who honor them; the carved ere ibeji keeps a dead twin in the family.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the farm and harvest
facets.core_claim: Orisha Oko makes the soil yield; his iron staff and his yams are the wealth of the farmer.

facets.facet_name: The one who spread the first earth at Ife
facets.core_claim: When Obatala was overcome by palm wine, Oduduwa took the bag of earth, poured it on the waters at Ife, and the hen scratched it out into the land.

facets.facet_name: First king and father of the Yoruba dynasties
facets.core_claim: Oduduwa is the first Ooni of Ife; every legitimate crown descends from him.

facets.facet_name: Personal deity of destiny
facets.core_claim: Before birth each soul kneels and chooses its Ori in heaven; the head one carries is the god one carries, and it is propitiated before all others.

facets.facet_name: Death, warrior of the ajogun
facets.core_claim: Iku is the chief of the ajogun who wage war on human life; he cannot be destroyed, only appeased and delayed through the sacrifices Ifá prescribes.

facets.facet_name: Earth-lord of smallpox and healing
facets.core_claim: Sakpata owns the earth; its grains erupt on the skin as smallpox when he is offended and he withdraws them when he is appeased.

facets.facet_name: Thunderer who punishes wrongdoing
facets.core_claim: Xevioso hurls thunderstones at those who lie and steal and sends the rain that makes the fields fertile.

facets.facet_name: Iron, the tool of creation
facets.core_claim: Gu is the cutting tool of Mawu-Lisa; with him the earth was made habitable and humanity received the arts of iron.

facets.facet_name: Serpent who carries and encircles the world
facets.core_claim: Aido-Hwedo bore the creator in his mouth and now lies coiled beneath the earth, tail in mouth, so it does not sink into the sea; if he ate his tail the world would end.

facets.facet_name: Master of the sea
facets.core_claim: Agbe rules the ocean and the vodun of the waters; offerings are given to him on the shore.

facets.facet_name: The written destiny revealed by divination
facets.core_claim: Mawu wrote each person's destiny; Fa is that writing, and through the palm nuts the diviner reads it so people can live in accord with it.

facets.facet_name: River god of war and thunder
facets.core_claim: Tano is the strongest of Nyame's sons, given the river and its people; he fights for them and judges their wrongdoing.

facets.facet_name: Elder son tricked of his inheritance
facets.core_claim: Nyame meant to give Bia the fertile land, but the goat told Tano to go first; Bia received the barren country instead.

facets.facet_name: Forest monster and ally of witches
facets.core_claim: Sasabonsam lies in wait in the tall trees and catches with his hooked feet those who walk the forest alone.

facets.facet_name: Trickster of war and chaos
facets.core_claim: Ekwensu stirs violence and cunning; warriors invoke his frenzy, and the wise keep him at a distance once the fight is over.
facets.scholarly_note: Christian missionaries chose Ekwensu to translate "Devil" in the Igbo Bible, a move many Igbo traditionalists reject as a mistranslation of an ambivalent trickster.

facets.facet_name: God of the strong right hand
facets.core_claim: Ikenga is the power of a man's own right hand to succeed; through it he acts in the world and his Chi works.

facets.facet_name: Spirit who calls the diviner
facets.core_claim: Agwu gives the dibia sight and medicine; to the one who resists his call he sends confusion and illness.

facets.facet_name: The sun, eye of Chukwu
facets.core_claim: Anyanwu sees everything under heaven and lights the path of those who live rightly.

facets.facet_name: Personal destiny-spirit
facets.core_claim: Each person's chi is a spark of Chukwu that chose their destiny with them; no one rises beyond the will of their chi.

facets.facet_name: High creator God
facets.core_claim: Osanobua made all things and stands above the gods; his children rule the realms of water, earth and death on his behalf.

facets.facet_name: King of the waters, giver of wealth and children
facets.core_claim: Olokun rules a palace beneath the waters as the Oba rules on land; he sends children, riches and health to those who keep his altars.

facets.facet_name: King of death
facets.core_claim: Ogiuwu owns death; all who die enter his realm, and his shrine is fed with blood.

facets.facet_name: God of the shining mountain
facets.core_claim: Ngai made all things and dwells on Kirinyaga; he gave the land to Gikuyu and is approached under the sacred fig.

facets.facet_name: First parents of the Kikuyu clans
facets.core_claim: Ngai showed Gikuyu the land from the mountain top and gave him Mumbi; from their daughters come all the clans.

facets.facet_name: Divinity who withdrew to the sky
facets.core_claim: Nhialic created all and once walked near people; after the first woman's hoe struck the sky he went far off, and now is reached through prayer and sacrifice.

facets.facet_name: Free-divinity of rain and lightning
facets.core_claim: Deng sends the rain and strikes with lightning; his name is the word for rain.

facets.facet_name: First woman and gardener
facets.core_claim: Abuk wanted more than the one grain a day Nhialic allowed; she pounded more, her pestle struck the sky, and he withdrew.

facets.facet_name: First man and power of the sun
facets.core_claim: Garang was made with Abuk and remains a power who seizes people with fevers and must be honored.

facets.facet_name: Spirit of the sky, everywhere like wind
facets.core_claim: Kwoth is like the wind, invisible yet everywhere; all things come from him and the lesser spirits are his refractions.

facets.facet_name: Supreme God above all spirits
facets.core_claim: Nzambi a Mpungu made the world and all its powers; he is beyond images, and all lesser force flows from him.

facets.facet_name: Spirit bound in a sacred object
facets.core_claim: A nkisi is a dead spirit made to work through medicines in a figure; each nail driven into the nkondi wakes it to enforce an oath or punish a wrong.

facets.facet_name: The water-boundary between living and dead
facets.core_claim: Kalunga is the shining water between the two worlds; to die is to go under it and to be born is to come back across it, as the sun does each day.

facets.facet_name: Spirits of springs, pools and rocks
facets.core_claim: The bisimbi inhabit sacred waters and stones; they guard the community whose land they live in and punish those who violate their places.

facets.facet_name: The rainbow tyrant
facets.core_claim: Nkongolo ate in public, married his sisters and ruled by force; he is the uncivilized kingship that true Luba royalty replaced.

facets.facet_name: Hunter who brought refined kingship
facets.core_claim: Mbidi Kiluwe hid when he ate and drank, revealing a dignity unknown to Nkongolo; from him comes the sacred blood of Luba kings.

facets.facet_name: Founder of sacred Luba kingship
facets.core_claim: Kalala Ilunga escaped Nkongolo's trap, returned with an army, and beheaded the rainbow king; his descendants are the bulopwe, the sacred rulers.

facets.facet_name: High God of rain who speaks from the caves
facets.core_claim: Mwari created people and sends the rain; his voice answers petitioners from the shrine caves, and the land prospers when he is honored.

facets.facet_name: Royal ancestral spirit and guardian of the land
facets.core_claim: Nehanda is a guardian of the whole land; she possesses her mediums to guide the people and defend the soil of the ancestors.

facets.facet_name: Prophet-guardian spirit
facets.core_claim: Chaminuka sees what is to come and speaks through his medium to warn and protect the people.

facets.facet_name: The one who appeared first
facets.core_claim: uMvelinqangi was before everything; thunder is his voice and he is greater than every ancestor.

facets.facet_name: Heavenly princess of rain and crops
facets.core_claim: Nomkhubulwana walks the fields veiled in mist; where she is honored by the young women the maize grows and the rain falls.

facets.facet_name: Ancestors of the lineage
facets.core_claim: The amadlozi live on and care for their homestead; neglect angers them, and honoring them brings health and luck.

facets.facet_name: Witch-sent malicious sprite
facets.core_claim: The tokoloshe is a familiar that the umthakathi (witch) sends to bite, frighten and sicken; the inyanga's medicine drives it away.

facets.facet_name: Creator of the defended world
facets.core_claim: Qamata made the earth and defended it from the dragon of the sea; travelers honor him by adding a stone to the roadside cairn.

facets.facet_name: Creator in the eastern sky
facets.core_claim: ǂGao!na made all things and sends rain and game; the stories of his foolish early deeds are told alongside prayers to him.

facets.facet_name: Trickster who shoots arrows of death
facets.core_claim: ǁGauwa and the dead shoot the small arrows that bring misfortune; the healers in trance draw them out and argue the dead away.

facets.facet_name: Rain-giving god of the red dawn
facets.core_claim: Tsui-ǁGoab gives rain and life; he battled ǁGaunab many times, was wounded in the knee, died and rose again, and finally triumphed.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the dark sky and death
facets.core_claim: ǁGaunab wars against the rain-giver and kills people; though defeated and thrown down, he still lurks in the dark to strike.

facets.facet_name: Hero of the many graves
facets.core_claim: Heitsi-eibib defeated the monster Ga-gorib and died and returned again and again; every cairn is one of his graves.

facets.facet_name: Reborn serpent-ancestor of the earth
facets.core_claim: Lébé was buried and returned as a snake; each night he licks the Hogon to give him the strength of the earth for the people.

facets.facet_name: River spirit who ordered the world
facets.core_claim: Faro descended as water and rain, restored the order Pemba had broken, and gave people speech, the calendar and the rules of life.

facets.facet_name: First creator who overreached
facets.core_claim: Pemba shaped the earth and the first woman, Musokoroni; he made himself a tree to be worshipped and claimed creation as his own.

facets.facet_name: First woman of disorder
facets.core_claim: Musokoroni refused Pemba and wandered the earth in frenzy; wherever she went she sowed both disorder and the first crops.

facets.facet_name: Supreme God of the Serer
facets.core_claim: Roog is the source of everything and is approached through the pangool ancestors; the saltigue read his will for the coming season.

facets.facet_name: Ancestral intercessor spirits
facets.core_claim: The pangool carry prayers to Roog and protect the families and lands that keep their shrines.

facets.facet_name: Creator and father of the gods
facets.core_claim: Katonda created the world and everything in it; the lubaale serve under him.

facets.facet_name: Lord of the lake and of plenty
facets.core_claim: Mukasa calms the lake, sends the fish and grants children; he asks no blood, only offerings of cattle and beer.

facets.facet_name: War god of Buganda
facets.core_claim: Kibuka flew above the battle in a cloud and shot the enemy with arrows; Buganda won while he was at its side.

facets.facet_name: Death who followed the first couple
facets.core_claim: Gulu warned Kintu and Nambi not to turn back; Nambi did, and Walumbe came with them. His brother Kayikuuzi chased him but he hid in the ground.

facets.facet_name: First man and founding king
facets.core_claim: Kintu came with one cow and won Nambi by completing the impossible tasks Gulu set; the kings of Buganda descend from him.

facets.facet_name: Mother of fertility
facets.core_claim: Ateetee is the women's protector; married women gather to sing to her and she grants children and safety in birth.

facets.facet_name: Creator who gives the breath of life
facets.core_claim: Zanahary made all and gives the breath; prayers begin with him before the ancestors.

facets.facet_name: The ancestors of the famadihana
facets.core_claim: The razana watch over their descendants and are owed tombs, offerings and the periodic rewrapping of their bones.

facets.facet_name: Lion god of war and royal victory
facets.core_claim: Apedemak, splendid god, lion of the south, gives the king victory over his enemies and feeds the land; Meroitic kings built temples to him as their own god.

facets.facet_name: Ram-headed Amun who chooses the kings
facets.core_claim: Amun of Napata dwells inside the holy mountain; he names the king by oracle, and the king rules as his son.

facets.facet_name: God of procreation and doorway guardian
facets.core_claim: Sebiumeker is the begetter, standing at the gate of the temple to guard what lies within.

facets.facet_name: The good companion and hunter-guardian
facets.core_claim: Arensnuphis accompanies and protects; he hunts and brings back the far-wandering goddess.

facets.facet_name: Ram-horned oracle god of the desert
facets.core_claim: Ammon speaks from his oasis sanctuary to all who make the desert crossing; kings seek his word and his sonship.

facets.facet_name: Bull god carried into battle
facets.core_claim: Gurzil, son of Ammon, goes before the tribe in battle in his bull image and gives his people courage.

facets.facet_name: Rain god who seeks his bride
facets.core_claim: Anzar dried up the springs until the girl he loved came to him; when they joined, the rain returned, and the rite of the Bride of Anzar renews that union.

facets.facet_name: Patroness against lightning and sudden death
facets.core_claim: Saint Barbara intercedes for those in danger from lightning, fire and explosion, for God avenged her with the thunderbolt.

facets.facet_name: Patron of lepers and the sick
facets.core_claim: Saint Lazarus, who suffered sores in this life and was comforted in the next, intercedes for the sick and the outcast.

facets.facet_name: Patroness of the harbor and seafarers
facets.core_claim: Our Lady of Regla watches over the harbor and all who travel by sea.

facets.facet_name: Keeper of the keys of heaven
facets.core_claim: To Peter were given the keys: what he binds on earth is bound in heaven, and he opens the gate to the blessed.

facets.facet_name: Warrior saint who slew the dragon
facets.core_claim: Saint George, armored for Christ, overcomes the dragon and defends the weak; soldiers call on him in battle.

facets.facet_name: Finder of lost things and patron of travelers
facets.core_claim: Saint Anthony restores what is lost and opens the way for the traveler and the poor.

facets.facet_name: Child pilgrim who aids prisoners and travelers
facets.core_claim: The Holy Child goes out by night with his basket and staff to feed prisoners and guide travelers; his worn shoes are the sign of his journeys.

facets.facet_name: Scarred Black Madonna, protectress of her people
facets.core_claim: Our Lady of Częstochowa, wounded in her image, defends her people and is crowned their Queen.

facets.facet_name: Patroness of Cuba who came on the waters
facets.core_claim: Our Lady of Charity calmed the sea for the three Juans and remains the mother of all Cubans.

facets.facet_name: Ransomer of captives
facets.core_claim: Our Lady of Mercy frees the captive; her white mantle shelters all who are bound.

facets.facet_name: Virgin of the candle and the purification
facets.core_claim: Our Lady of Candelaria carries the light of Christ presented in the Temple.

facets.facet_name: Warrior apostle on the white horse
facets.core_claim: Santiago rides into battle for the faithful; Christ named him a son of thunder.

facets.facet_name: Forerunner and baptizer
facets.core_claim: John prepares the way and baptizes with water for repentance.

facets.facet_name: Bishop who drove out the serpents
facets.core_claim: Saint Patrick, with his staff, banished the serpents from Ireland and planted the faith.
