canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Burkert, The Orientalizing Revolution. The structural and mythological parallels are extensively documented.

basis: Melqart is the Phoenician dying-rising king — attested annual awakening (egersis) ceremony
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Bonnet, Melqart. The Tyrian Herakles identification with Greek Heracles is documented in Herodotus.

basis: Plotinus' One directly influenced Kabbalistic Ein Sof through Jewish Neoplatonism
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Katz, Jewish Philosophers and the New Age. The Kabbalistic Ein Sof is a transformation of Plotinian thought through Jewish mysticism.

basis: Both are threshold guardians who must be propitiated first before any other deity is approached
Both are the sun as supreme cosmic king — Sol Invictus as Rome's late attempt at solar monotheism parallels Ra's supremacy in Egypt
Both personify time as the ultimate devourer — Kali as Mahakala, Zurvan as Boundless Time
Both are autonomous warrior goddesses who fight for cosmic order — neither is a consort
Both undergo violent dismemberment that generates cosmic abundance
Both must be invoked/propitiated before all other deities — lords of beginnings
Both are the most beloved deity whose violent death triggers cosmic catastrophe
Both are the returning god of a new world after the destruction of the old
Both are killed to generate agricultural renewal — the dying-god cycle in its most explicit agricultural form
Both are the divine wisdom figure who knows all destinies and transmits this knowledge through an oracle/writing system
Both are the great mother of the divine family who protects and nurtures through dangerous waters
Both are the supreme goddess of both love and war — the same divine feminine encompasses erotic power and martial fury
Tlaloc (Aztec) and Chaac (Maya) are the Mesoamerican rain-god — same functional role, shared iconographic tradition, different peoples
Both are the supreme illuminating wisdom that transforms ignorance — Ptah through the divine word, Vairochana through primordial light
Both ARE the earth — not rulers of it but the earth itself as a living divine body
Both destroy to create — their annihilating power is inseparable from their generative force
Both are supreme creators who completely withdrew from their creation — the deus otiosus pattern at its most extreme
Both destroy a failed human creation with a flood and recreate — the reset cosmogony
Varuna (Rita) and Ahura Mazda (Asha) are reflexes of the same PIE cosmic-order-keeper *H₂rtós
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Dumezil demonstrated the Mitra-Varuna / Ahura-Mazda structural parallel. The PIE cosmic law (*h₂rtos) survives as Sanskrit rita, Avestan asha.

basis: Indra slaying Vritra IS the Vedic instance of the PIE *Perkwunos vs. *Ngwhi dragon-slayer formula
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: West, Indo-European Poetry and Myth (2007). The Vritra myth shares deep structural and etymological features with the Baltic Perkunas/Velnias conflict.

basis: Both are the divine messenger who carries communications between the human and divine realms
The Amesha Spentas influenced Jewish angelology which influenced Kabbalistic sefirot
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Boyce, History of Zoroastrianism. The transmission through Babylonian exile is documented.

basis: Guanyin IS the feminized Avalokitesvara, who is structurally identical to Tara — both are the compassionate bodhisattva of liberation
Both are the high god who rules the divine council through authority and delegation rather than direct action
Both are the most widely practically worshipped deity — present at every gate, every beginning, every transaction
Both are sky fathers whose union with earth mothers creates the world; both lose their consort to the underworld
Both are storm gods who slay a multi-headed cosmic serpent — the Japanese instance and the Hittite instance of the same dragon-slayer formula
Perun and Perkunas are direct linguistic cognates — both = PIE *Perkwunos
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: The etymological identity is established. Both preserve the PIE thunder-god + cosmic serpent combat formula.

basis: Both are dying-rising gods whose annual death and return marks the agricultural cycle
Both are goddesses of the sacred eternal fire tended by virgin/consecrated women
Both are the Cosmic Human whose body/form is the structural template of the universe
Both are the structured divine realm of emanations through which the Absolute creates — 30 Aeons vs 10 Sefirot
Barbelo and Sophia are the same divine feminine principle in different Gnostic systems — the highest feminine Aeon
Papa Legba IS the Vodou transformation of Yoruba Eshu/Elegba — direct diasporic transmission
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: The Yoruba Elegba became Haitian Legba through the Middle Passage. Deren, Divine Horsemen.

basis: Both are the Mesoamerican/Andean divine civilizer who departs eastward/into the sea and is expected to return
Both are hidden supreme deities known only to initiates, preceding all creation and description
Both are spider creator-tricksters — the spider as cosmic weaver appears independently in Oceanic and African traditions
Varuna and Ahura Mazda are reflexes of the same PIE sovereign sky god *Deywos — the most documented PIE parallel
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Dumezil, Mitra-Varuna (1948). The Mitra/Mithra correspondence completes the pair.

basis: Both are ecstatic great mother goddesses whose rites involve dissolution of ego and conventional limits
Both are dying-rising consorts of great mother goddesses — Frazer's documentation
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Frazer, The Golden Bough, documents the Attis-Osiris-Adonis dying-rising complex explicitly.

basis: Both perform a cosmic slaying from which life springs — Mithras the bull, Indra the dragon
Both are the hidden absolute that manifests through a visible form — Amun (hidden) + Ra (sun), Ein Sof + Sefirot
Both are solar deities whose disappearance brings cosmic darkness and whose return brings light
Both create through thought/word — the mind as the primary creative instrument
Both govern the crossroads as the sacred threshold — propitiated first, intermediary between worlds
Both are the divine principle of ordered wisdom expressed through oracular speech and writing
Both goddesses embody the seasons — their emotional/physical state IS the seasonal cycle
Both are the dark destroyer who opposes the light-bringer in a cosmic dualism
Both are the withdrawn sky creator of East and West African peoples respectively
Both are the sacred fire goddess who is the supreme deity of her tradition
Zeus Horkios (of oaths) and Varuna are both the PIE cosmic-oath-keeper — *H₂rtos
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Dumezil, Indo-European Heritage in Rome and India.

basis: Both are corn deities whose death-and-resurrection is the origin of agricultural abundance — Cherokee and Mayan independent developments
Both are spider trickster-creators — independent developments of the spider as cosmic weaver
Late Hellenistic Isis as universal Queen of Heaven directly shaped early Marian theology, especially in Egypt
Hermes Trismegistus IS Thoth in the Hellenistic syncretism — the Egyptian wisdom god in Greek dress
Both are the rebellious first creation whose disobedience corrupts subsequent reality
Both refuse divine command — Iblis refuses to prostrate before Adam, Lilith refuses to lie beneath Adam. The rebellion of created equality.
Ishtar is Inanna in Akkadian — direct cultural continuity with regional differentiation
Both are the impersonal cosmic moral order that legitimizes rulers and structures reality
Both are deliberately constructed syncretic supreme beings — explicit synthesis of multiple religious traditions
Both are the ancestral spirit beings who maintain household and community well-being
Both are the sun whose daily victory over darkness/chaos requires sustained ritual support to continue
Both involve dismemberment of the feminine divine — though in opposite valences (victim vs. self-sacrifice)
Both are powerful lunar deities in Mesoamerican-Andean coastal cultures
The Olmec Dragon is the iconographic ancestor of Quetzalcoatl — Mesoamerican religious continuity over 2000+ years
Both are supreme creators who exist alone before creation — Hopi and Dogon independent developments of the apophatic supreme
Both are Caribbean/northern South American water-mother goddesses who emerge from sacred bodies of water
Both embody the destructive force of insatiable consumption/desire that traps and devours souls
Both are the eschatological warrior-savior who appears at the end of a corrupt age
Yama and Ymir derive from PIE *yemo (twin) — both first beings sacrificed to create the cosmos
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: Bruce Lincoln, Myth, Cosmos, and Society. The PIE first-twin cosmogony is preserved in Indo-Iranian Yama-Yima and Norse Ymir.

basis: Both are the primordial cosmic being whose body becomes the universe — Chinese and Indian developments
Both are the divine judge who determines the fate of the dead by weighing/measuring their lives
Both are the cosmic serpent of chaos that threatens the cosmos and is eternally opposed by the divine champion
Both are the bound divine adversary who will break free at the eschatological climax
Both are the three weaving Fates — PIE inheritance of the triple-weaver concept
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: The triple Fates appear across IE traditions — Norse Norns, Greek Moirai, Roman Parcae, Baltic Laimas. PIE origin probable.

basis: Both are dying-and-rising gods of ecstatic mystery cults — Greek and Phrygian developments
Both are the divine rebel against the supreme deity for the sake of humanity (or against humanity's elevation)
Ushas and Eostre are direct PIE cognates from *h₂éwsōs — Vedic Dawn = English Easter
canonical_parallels.scholarly_note: The most direct PIE etymological survival — both names derive from *h₂éwsōs.

basis: Both are the god of oaths who maintains the human bonds that sustain society
Both are collectives of divine emanations each representing a path/aspect of spiritual fulfillment
Sun Wukong's monkey-form and powers are influenced by Indian Hanuman through Buddhist transmission
Kamala IS Lakshmi in her tantric Mahavidya form — direct identification
Both hang on a cosmic tree/cross as self-sacrifice to obtain redemptive power
Both are fierce feminine war-death goddesses who hover over the battlefield as ravens/skulls
Both are sacred vessels/plants whose consumption grants divine inspiration or immortality
Both are divine physicians whose power to heal extends to raising the dead — causing theological crisis
Both are martyred sons of the divine whose death becomes the redemptive center of their faith tradition
Direct PIE cognates — *h2ewsos in Greek (Eos) and Sanskrit (Ushas)
Both are creator goddesses who become queens of the dead — the feminine who governs both creation and death
Mercury was identified with Celtic Lugus (= Lugh) and Germanic Wotan — the universal messenger-trickster
Rita (Sanskrit), Asha (Avestan), and Maat (Egyptian) are independent expressions of the same archaic truth-order concept
Erzulie Freda is the Haitian transformation of Oshun — direct diaspora transmission
Both are the mystical identity of individual soul with the divine absolute — Eckhart and Advaita independently arrive at the same insight
Both are the adversary with genuine greatness — Ravana the devoted Shiva worshipper, Loki the gods' companion who turns
The court accuser of Job and Zechariah becomes the personal Accuser of Revelation 12:10 who accuses the brethren before God
Septuagint renders śāṭān as diabolos, the source of "devil"
Both test human fidelity before God
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Hebrew Bible satan is a subordinate functionary, not God's cosmic enemy; the shift is gradual across the Second Temple period.

basis: Arabic shayṭān is cognate with Hebrew śāṭān and was likely transmitted through Aramaic/Ethiopic usage
Both accuse and test humanity under God's permission
Jubilees makes Mastema provoke God to test Abraham as the satan provokes God to test Job
Both act only with divine permission
Both are named from the root "hostility/opposition"
In Numbers 22 the Angel of YHWH himself stands "as a satan" against Balaam
Shows satan as a role an envoy of God can fill
The War Scroll says God made Belial "for the pit, an angel of mastema (hostility)"
Both lead the evil spirits that test and harm Israel for a fixed time
Paul uses Beliar as the opposite of Christ, i.e. as a name for Satan
Both rule the present age of darkness until defeated
The Community Rule's two spirits of truth and deceit resemble the Zoroastrian twin spirits
Both lead a camp of darkness opposed to the camp of light until a final victory
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Persian influence on Qumran dualism is a hypothesis; the Qumran spirits are both created by God, unlike Zoroastrian Angra Mainyu.

basis: A cosmic adversary who rules or corrupts the world for a limited age
Both are defeated in a final eschatological battle
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Possible Persian influence on Jewish and Christian demonology after the exile is debated; the Christian Devil remains a creature, not an independent principle.

basis: In the Life of Adam and Eve Satan is cast out for refusing to worship Adam; the Qurʾān tells the same of Iblīs
Both fall through pride at the creation of humanity
Iblīs is commonly derived from Greek diabolos; al-Shayṭān from śāṭān
Both tempt humanity to disobey God until the Day of Judgment
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam presents Iblīs as one of the jinn rather than a fallen angel in most readings.

basis: Jerome's Vulgate translates Hebrew hêlēl as "lucifer"
The fall from heaven for wanting to be like the Most High is carried over intact
A star-god attempts to take the throne on Zaphon, the divine mountain in the north
He fails and descends to rule below (earth / Sheol)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The connection is widely argued but not certain; Mark S. Smith, The Early History of God.

basis: Origen and later fathers read Isaiah 14 as the fall of the Devil
Lucifer becomes the pre-fall name of Satan
"I will be like the Most High" parallels the archon's boast "I am God and there is no other"
Both are powers whose pride over-reaches the true God
The same Morning Star figure, revalued from proud rebel to liberator
Luciferians read the fall as an act of illumination
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Modern Luciferianism (late 20th c.) reinterpreting the Christian Lucifer
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christian tradition sees the same act as the origin of evil.

basis: A light/fire-bringer who gives humanity knowledge against the will of the sovereign god
Punished or demonised for that gift
ʿAthtar is the Semitic cognate of Ishtar
Both are tied to the Venus star in parts of their range
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Cognate names, but the Ugaritic Athtar is male and has a different mythic role.

basis: Personified Dawn who opens the day
Born of the high gods and paired with the evening
The Gospels' Beelzeboul is the god of Ekron renamed as prince of demons
The Hebrew deformation "lord of flies" is preserved in the variant Beelzebub
Jesus answers the charge "by Beelzebul" with "if Satan casts out Satan", treating them as one
Both command the demons
zbl bʿl, "Baal the Prince", is a title of Baal Hadad at Ugarit
Baal Zebub is a local Baal of Ekron consulted for healing
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether Ekron's god was Hadad or a distinct local Baal is uncertain.

basis: Rabbinic texts call Samael "chief of all the satans" and make him the tempter in Eden
The Ascension of Isaiah uses Sammael alongside Satan and Beliar for the same ruler of this world
Gnostic texts give Samael as a name of the chief archon
Hypostasis of the Archons glosses Samael as "god of the blind"
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Gnostic usage borrows a Jewish angel name and reverses its target onto the creator.

basis: Kabbalistic texts pair Samael and Lilith as king and queen of the demonic realm
Both seduce and endanger humans
Samael rules the qelippot, the Sitra Achra that mirrors the holy sefirot
Both define a dark counterpart to the divine emanations
Both are the angel of death who takes each soul at its appointed time
Both act strictly under God's command
Islamic exegesis gives Iblīs's name before his fall as ʿAzāzīl
Both are rebellious angelic figures expelled from heaven
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The name ʿAzāzīl is reported in exegetical traditions (e.g. from Ibn ʿAbbās) and is not in the Qurʾān; the roles differ.

basis: Both are bound by Raphael in a desert place (Dudael; Upper Egypt)
Both are destructive spirits neutralised by angelic binding
Raphael is the agent of the binding that is Azazel's fate
The same scene seen from binder and bound
Both refuse to bow before Adam out of loyalty/pride toward God alone
Yazidism vindicates the refusal; Islam condemns it
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The shared motif is the root of outsiders' identification of Tawûsî Melek with Iblīs, which Yazidis reject.

basis: Both are angelic rulers of this world
Outsiders equated the Peacock Angel with Satan; Yazidis venerate him as God's faithful chief angel
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Polemical identification by Muslim and Christian neighbours and 19th-c. Western travellers; rejected by Yazidis
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: A polemical misidentification, not a Yazidi teaching; it has been used to justify persecution, including the 2014 genocide.

basis: Yazidis hold that Tawûsî Melek appeared in human form as Sheikh ʿAdī
Both are the centre of Yazidi devotion at Lalish
The Temple worships the same Egyptian Set, keeping the name Sutekh
It values the outsider-adversary qualities that Egyptian myth gave him
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Temple of Set, founded by Michael Aquino, 1975 (The Book of Coming Forth by Night)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Egyptian Set was also a protector of Ra; the Setian reading draws selectively on his adversary role.

basis: The Temple holds that "Satan" is a Hebrew distortion of the name Set
Both are the Prince of Darkness who sets himself apart from the cosmic order
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Temple of Set, founded by Michael Aquino, 1975
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The etymology Set → Satan is a Setian claim; linguists derive śāṭān from a Hebrew root meaning "oppose".

basis: The Temple of Set split from the Church of Satan in 1975
It kept the LaVeyan emphasis on self-deification but made the Prince of Darkness a real being
canonical_parallels.source_tradition: Church of Satan → Temple of Set (1975 schism)

basis: A venerated adversary who gives humanity self-aware illumination
Both frame the path as self-deification
LaVey took the Christian Adversary as a symbol and inverted its valuation
The Satanic Bible's Infernal Names come from Christian demonology
Same name and adversarial role
LaVeyans treat Satan as a symbol; theistic Satanists as a real being
Theistic Satanists hold that the being they venerate is the biblical Satan
The fall is reread as liberation rather than sin
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christian theology regards the same being as wholly evil.

basis: Both are non-theistic: Satan as symbol, not being
The Satanic Temple emphasises the rebel against tyranny, LaVeyans the carnal self
The rebel who defies an arbitrary sovereign for the sake of humanity
Both are literary heroes of the Romantic tradition of rebellion
The Satanic Temple's bronze is modelled directly on Lévi's 1856 Baphomet
Both depict the winged goat-headed androgyne as union of opposites
primary_text_evidence: Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (frontispiece)

basis: The Church of Satan's Sigil of Baphomet uses the goat head of Lévi's figure within an inverted pentagram
The goat-image migrates from occult symbol to Satanic emblem
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Lévi insisted Baphomet was not the Devil.

basis: Horned, goat- or stag-headed figure of nature's power
Both are read as symbols of balance and vitality rather than evil
The horned Devil of Christian art and the horned god share an iconography partly derived from Pan
Wiccans reject the identification of their God with Satan
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The early-20th-c. theory that the witch trials' "Devil" was a surviving horned god is rejected by historians.

basis: Isaiah 27:1 repeats the Ugaritic epithets "fleeing serpent, twisting serpent" word for word
The names ltn and liwyātān are the same word
The sea-dragon whose defeat founds cosmic order
Divine warrior splits/crushes the monster of the waters
Hostile sea defeated by the storm/divine warrior
Psalm 74 joins the splitting of Yam (sea) with the crushing of Leviathan
Litan belongs to Yam's host of the sea
Both are slain by Baal and Anat
Revelation's seven-headed dragon, "the ancient serpent", reuses the Leviathan image for Satan
Both are slain/bound by God at the end
The sea monster cut in pieces at creation
Cosmic order established by the divine warrior's victory
Parallel names for the primordial sea enemy in Isaiah and Job
Both are pierced/crushed by YHWH
Paired primordial beasts of land and sea
Both reserved as food for the righteous at the end
The dragon of the dark waters hostile to the divine
Bound or subdued by the forces of light
Greek writers describe Carthaginian child sacrifice by fire to "Kronos"
Both are associated with the devouring of children
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Greek interpretatio of the Punic Baal Hammon; whether biblical Molech is a god or a rite is debated.

basis: The Carthaginian tophet sacrifices dedicated to Tanit and Baal Hammon match the biblical Topheth rite
Both involve infant offerings recorded as mlk/molk
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Interpretation of the tophet remains contested.

basis: Personified Destruction/Death ruling the underworld
Both devour the living
Both are an end-time deceiver posing as Messiah, slain by Jesus at his return
Arabic dajjāl corresponds to Syriac Christian daggālā "deceiver", used of the Antichrist
Crowley adopted the title To Mega Therion, the Beast 666 of Revelation 13
He inverted the Beast into the prophet of the new Aeon
Babalon is the Whore of Babylon riding the seven-headed beast, revalued as sacred
Cup, beast and scarlet are taken directly from Revelation 17
Jerome notes that both "Abraxas" and "Meithras" add up to 365
Both are tied to the cycle of the year
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: An isopsephic coincidence noted in antiquity, not proof of a shared cult.

basis: Composite animal-headed ruler with serpent body
Both preside over the planetary heavens
The great prince of Daniel is the captain of the hosts of Revelation
Both fight God's battles against hostile powers
The Qurʾān names Mīkāl beside Jibrīl as angels brought near
The name is the Arabic form of Mikhaʾel
Divine champion who defeats the dragon and secures heaven
Revelation's war in heaven reuses the combat myth
A heavenly figure who weighs the soul after death
Decides admission to the realm of light
Jehovah's Witnesses hold that the pre-human Jesus is Michael the Archangel
Both lead the heavenly army against Satan
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society (Jehovah's Witnesses), 20th c.
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mainstream Christianity rejects the identification.

basis: The same Jesus of the New Testament, read as God's first creation rather than co-eternal God
Both are the Word through whom all else was made
canonical_parallels.source_tradition: Bible Student movement (C. T. Russell) from Protestant Christianity

basis: The interpreter of Daniel's visions is the angel of the Annunciation
Both announce God's decrees to chosen humans
Jibrīl is the Arabic form of Gavriʾel
The angel of revelation in all three traditions
The Qurʾān calls the bringer of revelation Rūḥ al-Qudus, "the Holy Spirit", which exegetes identify with Jibrīl
Both convey divine revelation to prophets
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam does not regard the Spirit as divine; the shared title has different theological meaning.

basis: An angelic intelligence dictates a scripture word for word to a prophet
Revelation in a set place and time (Hira; Cairo 1904)
Divine messenger who carries the decrees of the high god to humans
Mediates between the heavenly court and chosen mortals
Divine healer of blindness and disease
Healing linked to sacred remedy (fish gall; snake and dream)
Heavenly reckoner of the sun, moon and calendar
Reveals the measures of time to scribes
Angel set over the prison of the damned
Executes divine judgment on the condemned
A divine herald whose horn-blast announces the end of the world
Waits in readiness for the final moment
Yazidi lists name the Seven Angels with Islamic archangel names including ʿAzrāʾīl
Shared Islamic angelology
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The named list comes from texts of disputed authenticity.

basis: Jibrāʾīl appears among the Seven Angels in Yazidi lists
Both belong to a council of chief angels under God
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The named list comes from texts of disputed authenticity.

basis: A heptad of divine beings emanated from the high God to govern creation
Each member oversees part of the created order
primary_text_evidence: Yasht 19.16-18 (the seven Amesha Spentas of one mind)
Greater Bundahishn 1 (Ohrmazd creates the six Amesha Spentas)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Possible Iranian substrate in Yazidism; no direct transmission is proven.

basis: The Talmud applies "my Name is in him" (Exodus 23:21) to Metatron
Both bear the divine Name as God's chief agent
Early Christian writers identified the Angel of the LORD with the pre-incarnate Word
Both make the invisible God visible
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: A Christian reading; Jewish tradition does not identify the Angel with a divine person.

basis: Later Kabbalah identifies Sandalphon with the transfigured Elijah, parallel to Enoch becoming Metatron
Both span earth and heaven
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Medieval kabbalistic identification, not Talmudic.

basis: Angels descend to earth, teach magic, and sin with a woman
Bound in a pit until judgment
Invisible intermediate spirits that can afflict humans
A realm of spirits between angels and humanity
The Spirit of God hovering over the waters becomes the third person of the Trinity
Hebrew rûaḥ ha-qōdeš is rendered pneuma hagion
Kardec identified the promised Consoler/Spirit of Truth with Spiritist revelation
Both fulfil John 14:16–26
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Allan Kardec, The Gospel According to Spiritism (1864)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christian churches reject the identification.

basis: Mary Baker Eddy taught that the promised Comforter is Divine Science
Both are the Spirit leading into all truth
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Mary Baker Eddy, Science and Health (1875)

basis: Mandaean Ruha bears the title Ruha d-Qudsha, "the Holy Spirit"
Mandaeism inverts the Christian Holy Spirit into a power of darkness
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Often read as Mandaean polemic against Christianity.

basis: Same biblical holy spirit
Trinitarians call it a divine person; Jehovah's Witnesses an impersonal force
Jah is the short form of YHWH found in Psalm 68:4 and Hallelu-jah
Same God of Israel, read through the King James Bible
canonical_parallels.source_tradition: Rastafari from the King James Bible

basis: "Jehovah" is a Latinised form of YHWH with the vowels of Adonai
Same covenant God, understood as unipersonal
The same Tetragrammaton God of the Pentateuch
Samaritans and Jews share the Torah but dispute the chosen place
Strict unipersonal monotheism rejecting the Trinity
God without partners or co-equals
Non-trinitarian one God, the Father
Jesus subordinate to God
God's essence is unknowable and beyond all attributes
Bahá'í theology grew from Shiʿi Islamic thought
God as first cause and supreme intelligence from which all derives
All beings proceed from and return toward that source
God as the only true reality behind appearances
Union of the soul with the divine ground
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Eddy's idealism and Eckhart's apophatic ground differ substantially.

basis: Eddy's Christ as "divine idea" reinterprets the Johannine Logos
Distinguishes the human Jesus from the eternal Christ
Ibn ʿArabī identifies the Muḥammadan Reality with the Perfect Human
Both are the mirror in which all divine names are manifest
A pre-existent principle through which creation came to be
Manifest in a historical messenger
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam rejects any divinity of Muḥammad; the parallel is structural only.

basis: Intercessor whose plea before God obtains mercy for believers
Devotion expressed by invoking blessings on the intercessor's name
The prophet through whom the definitive law is given
Belief in him is an article of faith
Expected end-time restorer who renews true worship and justice
Prophet-like figure, not God
John's Gospel shows a Samaritan woman expecting the Messiah who "will tell us everything"
Both are a coming prophet-redeemer
The Báb proclaimed himself the Qá'im, the promised Mahdi of Shiʿi Islam
Both inaugurate the end-time renewal
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: The Báb (1848 declaration at Tabriz); Bábí and Bahá'í Faiths
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Muslims reject the claim.

basis: Bahá'u'lláh proclaimed himself the return of Christ in the glory of the Father
Both are the promised redeemer of the last age
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Bahá'u'lláh (declaration 1863; letters to world rulers 1867–73)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Christians reject the claim.

basis: Bahá'ís identify Bahá'u'lláh with the Zoroastrian promised saviour (Shah Bahram)
Both bring the final renovation
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Bahá'í Faith (writings of Bahá'u'lláh and Shoghi Effendi)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Zoroastrian orthodoxy rejects the claim.

basis: Bahá'í writings identify Bahá'u'lláh with the coming Buddha Maitreya
Both are the future world-teacher
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Bahá'í Faith (Shoghi Effendi, 20th c.)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Buddhist traditions reject the claim.

basis: Both are prophet-lawgivers in a line from Abraham
Bahá'ís reinterpret "Seal of the Prophets" so that new Manifestations remain possible
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Islam holds prophecy ended with Muḥammad.

basis: Designated successor and authorised interpreter of the founder
Keeps the community united after the founder's death
A Fatimid/Ismaili leader withdraws into concealment and will return at the end
Druze occultation doctrine grows from Shiʿi Imamology
The first emanation from the One is the Universal Intellect
Druze cosmology inherits Ismaili Neoplatonism
Rastafari identify Haile Selassie I as the returned Christ in kingly character
Titles King of Kings and Lion of Judah from Revelation
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Early Rastafari preachers in Jamaica (Leonard Howell and others), 1930s
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Haile Selassie, an Ethiopian Orthodox Christian, did not claim this; Christian churches reject it.

basis: Leader calling a people out of bondage to a promised land
Popularly called "Black Moses"
The Ethiopian Covenant of Mercy is a form of Marian intercession
Mary obtains mercy for those who invoke her
Sheikh ʿAdī was a Sufi master; Yazidi veneration of him grows from the Sufi saint-pole idea
Both are living axes of divine presence
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Yazidism developed far beyond its Sufi origins.

basis: Withdrawn high god who delegates rule to a council of subordinate powers
The creator stands above the world his agents administer
Transcendent source beyond the material world from which the light-beings emanate
Untouched by the creator of matter
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mandaeism is related to but distinct from Sethian and Valentinian Gnosticism; see Birger Pearson, Ancient Gnosticism (2007).

basis: Descending revealer who brings saving knowledge from the realm of light
Defeats the powers of darkness and opens the way of ascent for souls
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mandaeism rejects Jesus; the parallel is the shared Gnostic redeemer pattern.

basis: Lower being who fashions the material world and the body of Adam
Cannot give the soul; life must come from the higher realm
The name Ptahil is often derived from Ptah
Both are craftsman-creators of the world
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Proposed etymology; the Mandaean figure is a flawed demiurge, unlike Ptah.

basis: Fallen feminine power who is mother of the world-rulers
Assists in fashioning humanity's body
Judgment of the dead by weighing at the threshold of the blessed realm
Only the pure soul is admitted to the realm of the blessed
Descent into the underworld to bind its powers and return victorious
The descent opens the way for souls to ascend
Descent through the gates of the underworld and triumphant return
A divine figure confronts the rulers of the dead in their own realm
Nuit is the sky-goddess Nut as shown arching over the Stele of Revealing
Both are the star-filled body of the sky
Hadit is drawn from the winged disk Behdety (Horus of Behdet) on the Stele
Solar-winged emblem of the god
Ra-Hoor-Khuit is the hawk-headed Re-Harakhty enthroned on the Stele of Revealing
Solar king of the gods
The two are the passive and active halves of Heru-ra-ha
Book of the Law presents them as one double god
Harpocrates, Horus the Child son of Isis, is taken over as the Thelemic Lord of Silence
Both are the child-form of Horus
Infinite circumference and infinitely small centre
Divine lovers whose union produces all things
One Goddess of many names, mother of nature
The Charge lists Isis among her names
The Charge of the Goddess names Diana among her names
Leland's Aradia makes Diana queen of the witches
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Charles Godfrey Leland, Aradia (1899); Gardnerian Wicca and Doreen Valiente's Charge (1950s)

basis: Triple-formed goddess
Tied to the moon, night and magic
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Wiccan Maiden-Mother-Crone is a 20th-c. formulation; Hekate's triple form is ancient but not identical.

basis: Wicca names Cernunnos as a name of the Horned God
Antlered lord of animals and fertility
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Gardnerian Wicca (Gerald Gardner, 1950s)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Ancient Cernunnos is known mainly from iconography; the Wiccan theology is modern.

basis: God who dies and rises with the agricultural year
Rules the land of the dead between
Wild, horned or animal-linked god of nature and ecstasy
Associated with death and renewal in the cycle of the year
God presents Behemoth and Leviathan side by side as creatures only he can master
Both display divine power over untameable creation
Both are kings of demons whom Solomon commands in the Testament of Solomon
Both rule hosts of afflicting spirits
A historical man held to be the human manifestation of a divine being
Medieval Islamic-world figure transformed by a later esoteric community
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Druze and Yazidi doctrines of manifestation differ and are unrelated historically.

basis: Sanskrit Dyaus Pitā continues PIE *dyēus ph2tēr phonologically and morphologically
Both are the bright day-sky addressed as 'father'
Both form a sky-father/earth-mother pair (Dyāvāpṛthivī)
Dyaus Pitā and Zeus Patēr (Latin Iuppiter) are exact cognate formulas from *dyēus ph2tēr
Both are sky-fathers of gods and men
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Cognates, not the same cult: Dyaus is nearly inactive in Vedic worship while Zeus is the ruling king of Olympus.

basis: Herodotus explicitly names Papaios as the Scythian Zeus
Both are sky-fathers paired with Earth
Both are ancestors of the royal line (Targitaos son of Zeus)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Herodotus' equation is interpretatio graeca; Scythian theology is known only through Greek eyes.

basis: Herodotus equates Api with Gē
Both are Earth-mothers wedded to Sky
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Interpretatio graeca in Herodotus 4.59.

basis: Both are the personified Earth, universal mother
Both are paired with Sky (Dyaus / Ouranos) as primordial parents
Earth-mothers paired with a sky-father in neighbouring Indo-Iranian traditions
Both mothers of the people's ancestors
Vedic Mitra and Bactrian Miiro/Iranian Mithra continue one Indo-Iranian god *Mitra, 'contract, alliance'
Both guard oaths and covenants
Both are linked with the sun and light
primary_text_evidence: Mitanni–Hittite treaty of Šattiwaza (c. 1380 BCE) invoking Mi-it-ra with Uruwana, Indara and the Nasatya
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Same inherited deity, developed differently: Vedic Mitra is a quiet companion of Varuṇa, Iranian Mithra a mighty warrior-judge of contract.

basis: Roman Mithras bears the Iranian god's name and Persian dress
Both are solar, invincible, and lords of oath/loyalty
Roman sources themselves call the cult Persian
primary_text_evidence: Plutarch, Life of Pompey 24 (Mithraic rites of the Cilician pirates)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: How much of the Roman mysteries continues Iranian Mithra worship is debated; the tauroctony and grade system have no Iranian counterpart and may be Roman innovations under a Persian name.

basis: Avestan Verethragna (Bactrian Orlagno) = Vedic vṛtrahán 'slayer of Vṛtra/resistance', Indra's chief epithet
Both embody victory over an obstructing foe
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: In Zoroastrianism Indra himself is demonized (Vendidad 10.9) while his epithet became an independent yazata — a split of one Indo-Iranian complex.

basis: Sanskrit agní, Latin ignis, Lithuanian ugnis and Old Church Slavonic ognĭ share one root
Both are the sacrificial fire as divine messenger
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Latin ignis is a cognate common noun, not a Roman deity; Roman cult fire was Vesta.

basis: Vedic Yama, Avestan Yima and Old Norse Ymir are cognate with *Yemo 'twin'
Yama is the first mortal who found the path to the realm of the dead
Both are the sacred fire personified as a god carrying worship
Ātar and Agni are parallel Indo-Iranian fire deities
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Names are not cognate (Ātar vs agni); the parallel is functional.

basis: Sogdian Wēšparkar continues Avestan Vayu uparō.kairya 'Vayu working in the upper region'
Avestan Vayu is cognate with Vedic Vāyu, wind and breath
Bactrian Oesho (Wēš) and Sogdian Wēšparkar are the same East Iranian wind god
Both are depicted with Śiva's attributes (trident, multiple heads/arms)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Some read Oesho as simply Śiva under a Bactrian epithet; the Vayu etymology is widely but not universally accepted.

basis: Oesho is shown with trident, bull, water-pot and multiple arms — standard Śaiva iconography
Kushan kings (Vima Kadphises) styled themselves devotees of Maheśvara
primary_text_evidence: Coins of Vima Kadphises and Vasudeva I

basis: Sogdian Buddhist translators render Mahādeva (Śiva) as Weshparkar
Panjikent images of Weshparkar use Śiva's three heads and trident
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: An identification by translation and iconography; the two gods have distinct origins.

basis: Sogdian Buddhist texts translate Indra-Śakra as Adbag
Both are king of the gods of heaven
Sogdian Buddhist translators render Brahmā as Zurvan (Zrwa)
Both are the eldest, highest god of a pantheon
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Translation equivalence chosen by Sogdian Buddhists, not a claim of common origin.

basis: Mongolian Qormusta derives from Sogdian Xurmazta, from Avestan Ahura Mazdā
Both head the benevolent heavenly host against a dark host
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The name traveled; the Mongolian figure is a chief sky-god, not the sole creator of Zoroastrian theology.

basis: Mongolian Buddhism identifies Qormusta with Indra-Śakra
Both rule a heaven of thirty-three gods
primary_text_evidence: Mongolian Buddhist translations of Indra as Qormusta

basis: Sakka is 'Śakra lord of the devas', Indra's Vedic epithet śakra 'mighty'
Both rule the Heaven of the Thirty-Three on Meru
Buddhism keeps Indra's kingship but makes him a disciple
Buddhist Mahābrahmā is the Brahmanical creator Brahmā
The Brahmajāla Sutta reframes his creator claim as a delusion of being first-born
Thai Phra Phrom is Brahmā as received through Theravāda and Brahmanical court ritual
Both four-faced high gods subordinate to the Buddha
Vaiśravaṇa ('son of Viśravas') is Kubera's patronymic
Both rule the yakṣas, guard the north and give wealth
canonical_parallels.source_tradition: Buddhist adoption of the Brahmanical Kubera

basis: Buddhist Yama Dharmarāja is the Vedic-Hindu Yama adopted as judge of the hells
Both judge the dead according to their deeds
Mahākāla 'Great Black/Time' is a name of Śiva
Buddhist Mahākāla keeps Śaiva features: third eye, skull ornaments, trident, cremation ground
Buddhist narratives tell of Śiva subdued and made protector
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Tibetan tradition regards Mahākāla as a wrathful emanation of Avalokiteśvara, not as Śiva; the derivation is historical, not doctrinal.

basis: Guanyin translates Avalokiteśvara ('Perceiver of the World's Sounds')
Both answer every call for help (Lotus Sūtra ch. 25)
The figure was feminized in China from about the 10th–12th c.
Newar Buddhists worship Bunga Dyah as Karuṇāmaya Avalokiteśvara
Both compassionate saviours who relieve suffering — here drought
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Hindus identify the same image with the Nāth yogi Matsyendranāth — a double identity typical of Kathmandu Valley religion.

basis: Gandharan reliefs depict Vajrapāṇi with Herakles' club-form vajra, lion skin and muscular nudity
Both are invincible divine protectors
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: An artistic borrowing in Greco-Buddhist Gandhara, not a theological identification.

basis: Vajrapāṇi 'vajra-in-hand' is also Indra's epithet
Both wield the thunderbolt as protector-warriors
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Buddhist texts sometimes conflate Vajrapāṇi with Śakra; later Vajrayāna makes them distinct.

basis: Bhairava is the terrible form emanated by Śiva himself
Same skull, dog and cremation-ground attributes
Bactrian/Sogdian Nana descends from Mesopotamian Nanaya, long syncretized with Inanna/Ishtar
Both are lion-associated queens of heaven bearing sun/moon or star symbols
The cult spread east via Achaemenid and Seleucid networks
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The source goddess is Nanaya, distinct from Inanna in early Sumer though identified with Ishtar from the 2nd millennium BCE.

basis: Both are goddesses enthroned on or riding a lion
Both are sovereign, martial great goddesses
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Direct influence of Nana's lion iconography on Durgā's has been proposed but is unproven.

basis: Vedic Rudra is the same god later called Śiva
Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad already names Rudra as Śiva the supreme
Both are archers whose arrows bring plague
Both are also healers who withhold the arrow when appeased
Viśvakarman offers all worlds in sacrifice (RV 10.81)
Puruṣa is sacrificed to form the world (RV 10.90)
Both hymns make cosmogony a sacrifice
Both are divine craftsmen-architects of the gods' dwellings and weapons
Both forge the storm-king's weapon and the gods' vessels
Both are artisans whose offspring cause trouble
Both are benevolent divine twins who bring healing/growth to humans
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Typological only; no historical link between Vedic and Haudenosaunee twins.

basis: RV 10.121's refrain resolves in its last verse: 'Prajāpati, no one but you encompasses all these'
Both are the one lord of creation at the beginning
Manusmṛti and the Purāṇas: Brahmā is born within the golden egg on the waters
The Vedic golden embryo becomes the classical creator's birth
Both cosmogonies begin with a cosmic egg from which the first being emerges
Both separate heaven and earth from the egg
The Brāhmaṇas identify Prajāpati with Puruṣa
Both are the creator whose self-sacrifice becomes the cosmos
Vedic Trita (and Avestan Thrita/Thraētaona) continue PIE *Tritós 'the Third'
All kill a three-headed monster and recover cattle
Both are obstructors split by Indra
Vala withholds the cows of light, Vṛtra the waters
Apām Napāt is often addressed as a form of Agni born in the waters
Both are fire hidden in water/lightning
Both are thundering storm-and-rain gods
A derivation of Parjanya from *Perkʷunos has been proposed
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The etymology is phonologically irregular and widely doubted; treat as possible only.

basis: Both guard roads and travellers
Both conduct the dead to the other world
Both protect herds and find lost things
Both are solar gods of the Veda
Savitṛ is the impelling power, Sūrya the visible disk
Sūrya and Hēlios (and Latin Sol) derive from PIE *sóh2wl̥ 'sun'
Both drive a horse-drawn chariot across the sky and see all deeds
Upaniṣads identify the moon as King Soma, food of the gods
The waning moon is Soma drunk by the gods
Both are male moon gods measuring the months
Hellenistic astrology's planet Jupiter was rendered in India as Bṛhaspati/Guru
Both are the great benefic planet
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: An astrological equation of planets, not of the gods' myths.

basis: Both name the red planet and carry martial character
The equation entered India with Hellenistic astrology
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Planetary equation only.

basis: Both attack and attempt to swallow the sun
Both are chaos-beings defeated but never destroyed
Durgā is created specifically to slay Mahiṣāsura
Boon allowing death only by a woman is fulfilled by the Goddess
Both are asura kings whose boons make them conquer heaven
Both are undone by the loophole in their boon
Narasiṃha's every paradox answers a clause of Hiraṇyakaśipu's boon
Liberator and tyrant in one story
Both proclaim themselves the only god
Both are flawed world-rulers overthrown by a higher reality
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Typological comparison only.

basis: Varāha slays Hiraṇyākṣa and lifts the Earth he submerged
Vāmana's three strides take the three worlds from Bali
Both sides keep dharma: Bali his promise, Viṣṇu cosmic order
Both are rulers of a lost golden age displaced by a new divine order
Both are sent to a lower realm
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Kronos' golden-age role is chiefly Hesiodic/Roman (Saturn); the parallel is thematic.

basis: Balarāma is the incarnation of Śeṣa
At his death the serpent leaves his body
Śeṣa-Ananta is Viṣṇu's serpent couch on the cosmic ocean
Both are primordial serpents of the cosmic waters
Śeṣa sustains the cosmos, Vṛtra withholds and must be slain
Puri tradition worships Jagannātha as Kṛṣṇa with Balabhadra and Subhadrā
Jayadeva's Gīta Govinda was composed for him
Vārkarī saints address Viṭṭhala as Kṛṣṇa
Rukmiṇī is his consort at Pandharpur
Veṅkaṭeśvara is Viṣṇu descended for the Kali age
The Āḻvārs sang him as Tirumāl (Viṣṇu)
Both bear the title Sāstā and Hariharaputra
Both are guardian gods of Kerala and Tamil lands
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether they are one deity or two related figures is debated by devotees and scholars.

basis: Khaṇḍobā is called Mārtaṇḍa Bhairava
Both are Śiva forms accompanied by dogs and worshipped as guardians
The Malhari Māhātmya presents Khaṇḍobā as Śiva incarnate to slay Maṇi and Malla
Both are fierce Śaiva guardians who expel evil spirits
Both receive meat and liquor offerings in folk practice
Karuppasāmi serves as Ayyanār's chief attendant at village shrines
Both ride horses guarding the boundary
Both goddesses both send and cool pox
Both are propitiated with cooling offerings (neem, cold food)
Tamil legend identifies Māriyamman with Renukā/Yellammā
Both arise from the story of the beheaded mother of Paraśurāma
Both divine bodies are dismembered
Their parts sanctify the world (cosmos / sacred land)
Garuḍa steals the amṛta from the gods; Odin in eagle form steals the mead of poetry
Both flights of an eagle carrying the drink of immortality/inspiration
Rigvedic eagle (śyena) bringing soma is the older Indic form
Garuḍa is the eternal enemy of the nāgas
A serpent king spreads his hoods over a meditating founder
Jain and Buddhist versions of the same motif
Mucalinda is a nāga king of the pan-Indian serpent folk
Manasā is queen of the snakes
Both send and avert snakebite and grant fertility
Both are serpent-hooded goddesses of protection
Sītā is born from the earth and returns into her mother Bhūmi
Rādhā is theologized as the śakti of Kṛṣṇa
Both are the feminine power inseparable from God
Both are divine messengers moving between worlds
Both are musicians and mischief-makers serving divine ends
Both are honoured as the primordial guru (ādi-guru)
Both are wandering ascetic teachers
Both are divine founders of medicine
Both are worshipped by physicians
Both are divine healers invoked against disease
Both embody irresistible desire that overpowers even gods
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Closer typological match is Eros/Cupid, whose record has no facet yet.

basis: Akilathirattu teaches that Rāvaṇa was a fragment of Kroni reborn in the Tretā Yuga
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: An Ayyavazhi theological identification not shared by other Hindu traditions.

basis: Both are the final avatāra who ends the Kali age
Both restore dharma
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Ayyavazhi presents Vaikuṇḍar as fulfilling the end-time role others assign to Kalki.

basis: The iṣṭaliṅga is Śiva in liṅga form, made personal and portable
Both founders reject caste and ritualism
Both teach devotion with honest work (kāyaka / kirat karo)
Both are formless, self-existent creators
Both are kings of heaven and thunder
Ahom kings, as descendants of Lengdon, were equated with Indra's line
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Hinduized Ahom court and Assamese Brahmins, 16th–18th c. CE (Buranji tradition)

basis: Chaṇḍī dī Vār (Dasam Granth) retells the Goddess's battles with the demons
Both are divine power destroying evil
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Mainstream Sikh theology reads Bhagautī as an attribute of Akal Purakh, not the Hindu goddess.

basis: The Royal Kumārī is the living vessel of Taleju
Taleju is worshipped as a form of Durgā; her temple opens at Dasaiñ (Durgā Pūjā)
Mahandeo's name is cognate with Mahādeva
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Kalasha god is not a form of Hindu Śiva; the name reflects shared Indo-Aryan vocabulary.

basis: Both are collective mother-goddess groups
Both protect and receive collective cult
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Typological; no historical connection.

basis: Both are tantric sets of forms of one reality arranged in directions
Each member transforms a specific state into wisdom
Both oppose the founder throughout his quest
Both are finally defeated by the founder's steadfastness
Both assault a meditating founder with storms and terrors on the eve of liberation
Both fail before perfect equanimity
Both founders are attacked during final meditation and sheltered by a serpent king
Bön and Nyingma both name the primordial Buddha Kuntu Zangpo (Samantabhadra)
Both are naked, sky-blue dharmakāya
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Direction of borrowing between Bön and Nyingma Dzogchen is contested.

basis: Both are the Great Mother of wisdom from whom the enlightened arise
Both called Mother of All Buddhas
Both are wrathful queen-protectors riding a mule over a sea of blood
Both are founding teachers of Tibetan religion who subdue local demons
Rival founding figures of Nyingma and Bön
Both are female demons who prey on children
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Contrast in outcome: Hārītī converts and becomes protector, Lilith remains a threat.

basis: Gandharan Hārītī and Kushan Ardochsho both hold the cornucopia of Greek Tyche
Both are mother-goddesses depicted with children who protect childbirth
Both epic heroes are performed by inspired bards who receive the epic in dreams
Both unite their people against enemies
Both give humanity its first laws, arts and social order
Umay protects the birthing woman; Albasty attacks her
Rites invoke Umay against Albasty
Both are female night-demons who attack women in childbirth and newborns
Both are warded off with amulets and names
Both goddesses bring the child's soul and protect childbirth
Both are mother-goddesses of birth in Siberian sky-father religions
Both are the feminine counterpart of the sky-god
Both are the sacred Earth paired with Tengri
Both are Mother Earth in sky-earth religions of North Asia
Both are benevolent creators residing in the upper heavens of a tiered sky
Both are given white offerings
Both titles mean 'Lord of the Aiyy / creator light'
Both white creator-lords of the sky
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Possibly the same Sakha deity under variant names; recorded attributions vary.

basis: Both sky-gods share the word num 'sky/upper'
Both send diving birds to bring up earth
Both are earth-diver creators of Siberian dualist cosmogony
Both are underworld lords opposing the sky-creator
Both send disease and take the dead
Both are death-lords who spoil the sky-god's creation
Both are the evil partner in the earth-diver creation who mars the work
Both rule the lower world
Both rule the lower world and devour souls
Both create the earth with a dualist rival brother
Both lead a malevolent host against a benevolent one
Khormusta's name derives from Ahura Mazdā, sharpening the parallel
Raven frees the sun/light from a container
Bering Strait raven cycle shared across Siberia and the Northwest Coast
Both are Raven creator-tricksters of the Chukotko-Kamchatkan peoples
Both Ravens are transformer-tricksters who shape the land
Both give fire to humans
Both are ambivalent powers outside the benevolent high gods
Both are youngest sons of the sky-father who carry messages between heaven and earth
Herodotus names the Scythian sword-god Ares
Both are war gods receiving blood sacrifice
Herodotus equates Argimpasa with Aphrodite Urania
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Interpretatio graeca; Argimpasa's investiture role has no Greek counterpart.

basis: Herodotus equates Thagimasadas with Poseidon
Both are gods of waters and horses
Herodotus equates Goitosyros with Apollo
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Interpretatio graeca; content of the Scythian cult unknown.

basis: Both are the first man and ancestor of a people
Both are sons of a sky/sun god
Both are hearth-fire goddesses of steppe peoples
Both stand at the centre of household and royal cult
Both are the sacred hearth fire at the centre of the home
Śani is the planet Saturn, identified in Hellenistic astrology with Kronos
Both are slow, dark, malefic powers of time and hardship
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Planetary equation only; the myths are unrelated.

basis: Yanluo is the Chinese transliteration of Yama-rāja
Same office: judge of the dead in the Buddhist underworld
Transmitted with Buddhist scriptures into China
primary_text_evidence: Scripture on the Ten Kings (Shiwang jing)
Chinese Buddhist translations rendering Yama as 閻羅

basis: Vedic/Hindu Yama, first mortal and lord of the dead, passed into Buddhism and then China
Both judge souls according to their deeds
Name preserved in transliteration
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Chinese figure is heavily bureaucratized and placed within the ten-court system, a Chinese development.

basis: Enma-ō is the Japanese reading of 閻魔王 / 閻羅王
Same judge of the Ten Kings system
Transmitted with the Ten Kings scriptures to Japan
Yeomra is the Korean reading of 閻羅
Same fifth-court judge in the Ten Kings scheme
Korean Siwangdo paintings reproduce the Chinese system
Japanese honji suijaku doctrine names Jizō as the original ground (honji) of Enma
The wrathful judge and the compassionate saviour are one being in two aspects
primary_text_evidence: Jizō Jūō-kyō (Japanese apocryphal Ten Kings sutra)

basis: Kannon is the Japanese name of Avalokiteśvara
Same vow to hear and answer all who call
Same thirty-three manifestations from Lotus Sutra ch. 25
Kannon and Guanyin share the Chinese name 觀音
Japanese cult received from China via Korea
Same saving response to those who call the name
primary_text_evidence: Kumārajīva's Chinese Lotus Sutra (406 CE), ch. 25

basis: Jizō is the Japanese name of Kṣitigarbha (地藏)
Same vow to save beings in the hells
Japanese emphasis on children develops from this role
Amida is the Japanese name of Amitābha
Same 18th Vow promising rebirth to those who call his name
Japanese Pure Land schools received the cult through China
Benzaiten (弁才天) translates Sarasvatī as goddess of eloquence
Both hold a stringed instrument and preside over speech, learning and music
Both originate as river goddesses
primary_text_evidence: Suvarṇaprabhāsa (Golden Light) Sūtra, chapter on Sarasvatī

basis: Daikokuten (大黒天) translates Mahākāla, "Great Black One"
Both protect monks and the Dharma
Mahākāla was already honored in monastic kitchens in Indian practice reported by Yijing
primary_text_evidence: Yijing, Record of Buddhist Practices (691 CE)

basis: Medieval Japanese shinbutsu-shūgō identified Daikoku with Ōkuninushi
Both carry a sack and are linked with abundance of the land
The two names share the reading "Daikoku/Ōkuni" (大国 / 大黒)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The identification rests partly on a homophone; it is a syncretic equation rather than a shared origin.

basis: Bonten (梵天) is Brahmā in Japanese Buddhism
In Buddhist texts Brahmā requests the Buddha to teach
Same deity subordinated to the Buddha
Taishakuten (帝釈天) is Śakra, Buddhist name of Indra

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The goddesses are cognate and were syncretised, but their local cults remained distinct.

basis: Herodotus says the temple of Aphrodite Ourania at Ascalon is the oldest, and that the Cyprian and Cytheran cults came from it
Phoenician Astarte cult at Kition and Paphos on Cyprus, Aphrodite's island

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Aphrodite also has Indo-European elements (daughter of Zeus, dawn-goddess traits); the derivation is partial.

basis: The Pyrgi tablets dedicate one temple in Etruscan to Uni and in Phoenician to Astarte

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Anahita's Avestan core (the heavenly river) is Indo-Iranian; the Ishtar features are a later Achaemenid layer.

basis: Armenian Anahit is the Iranian Anahita adopted with Zoroastrian-influenced religion

Both are worshipped as dying-and-revived gods
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Eshmun's story survives only in Damascius and may be shaped by the Attis myth.

basis: Roman African dedications call the god of the former tophets Saturnus

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Whether mlk names a god or a type of offering, and whether the tophets held sacrifices or burials, are both debated.

basis: The Idalion bilingual equates Resheph with Apollo (Resheph-mkl = Apollo Amyklos)

Primordial human prototype preceding ordinary humanity

basis: Highest transcendent source of light

basis: The sun conceived as a ship carrying divine light through the cosmos

Libyan war cult tied to the Ammon tradition

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Apedemak is an indigenous Kushite god, not a borrowing of Sekhmet.

Both are remembered as a lord who came from the west and founded rule

Both are creator gods acting in council with other gods

Both are wind gods and plumed serpents who descend from the sky
Feathered and avian serpent imagery appears in Olmec art (e.g., La Venta Monument 19)
Later feathered-serpent gods are widely taken to continue it

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The continuity from Olmec serpent imagery to Quetzalcoatl is an iconographic inference, not a textual one.

Both receive offerings for agricultural rain
Both are the principal rain and lightning gods of their peoples
Both are rain gods with goggle-eyed masks in Postclassic art
Both are central to agricultural ritual
Olmec were-jaguar imagery is often proposed as an ancestor of later rain-god iconography

Colonial sources call Itzamna the son of Hunab Ku, the one god
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Hunab Ku is attested only in colonial sources and may reflect missionary influence.

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Many linguists treat the resemblance as coincidental; English "hurricane" comes from the Taíno word via Spanish.

Guabancex is sometimes treated as the storm aspect of Atabey

Both bring light and make the land

In both, Coyote makes death permanent by his action or argument

Coyote opposes Earth Initiate's plan and brings death
Both make the earth from mud brought up from the primal water onto a turtle

Both are Algonquian transformer-heroes who shape the land and the animals
Glooscap destroys his destructive twin

The Thunderbirds war against the underwater panther

In Lakota thought Inyan is the first and eldest manifestation of the sacred

Apache White Painted Woman and Diné Changing Woman are the same Southern Athabaskan mother of the monster-slayer
Both are embodied by girls in the puberty ceremony (Na'ii'ees / Kinaaldá)
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Apache groups vary in naming her White Painted Woman or Changing Woman.

Both are gods of the sprouting maize

Both are moon gods whose light is diminished in the founding story of sun and moon

Both are spirit likened to air or wind, everywhere present
They are the paired first beings who order the Diné world
Both make dry land by spreading a handful of earth on the primordial waters
Both are San creator gods who are also foolish tricksters in the old stories

The clumsy moon-twin and the capable sun-twin complement each other

Greek writers name the Egyptian Set as Typhon

A shared root for the two names has long been proposed
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The Varuna–Ouranos etymology is old and widely doubted; treat it as a possibility, not a finding.

In the Rigveda, desire (kama) is the first seed of mind at creation, as Eros is among the first powers in Hesiod
Spanish missionaries used 'Supay' to translate 'the Devil' in Quechua catechisms
Supay rules the inner world of the dead, the realm the missionaries equated with hell
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: The equation is a missionary translation. In Andean tradition Supay is an ambivalent lord of the inner earth, not a principle of evil.

canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Before missionary use, Ekwensu was an ambivalent trickster and war power, not an evil adversary of God.

Both stand at the head of the spirit powers outside the missionaries' God
canonical_parallels.scholarly_caveat: Tornarsuk was the master of the shamans' helping spirits; the devil reading is a missionary recasting.

In Northwest Amazonian tradition he is the culture-hero lawgiver of the sacred flutes

canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Trinidad Orisha (Shango) tradition, 19th–20th century

Both are images of nature's generative force
canonical_parallels.syncretic_source: Éliphas Lévi, Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie (1854–56)

Venus as a male divinity in both pantheons

cosmological_frameworks.name: The Yuga Cycle (Hindu Cosmic Ages)
cosmological_frameworks.summary: Hindu cosmology divides each great cycle (mahayuga) into four ages: Satya Yuga (golden age, dharma at 100%), Treta Yuga (dharma at 75%), Dvapara Yuga (dharma at 50%), and Kali Yuga (the present age, dharma at 25%). At the end of the Kali Yuga, Kalki appears, the world is destroyed, and a new Satya Yuga begins. The cycles nest: 1000 mahayugas = 1 kalpa (a day of Brahma).

stages.name: Satya Yuga (Krita Yuga)
stages.character: Golden age. Truth, virtue, longevity. Beings live thousands of years. No need for laws — dharma is innate.
cross_tradition_parallels: Aztec previous suns (golden age of Quetzalcoatl)

stages.name: Treta Yuga
stages.character: Silver age. Sacrificial religion develops. Heroic age. The Ramayana is set here.

stages.name: Dvapara Yuga
stages.character: Bronze age. Decline of virtue. The Mahabharata is set at its end. Krishna's life closes this yuga.

stages.name: Kali Yuga
stages.character: The current age, traditionally begun in 3102 BCE (Krishna's departure). Spiritual darkness, materialism, short lives, moral decline. Ends with Kalki's appearance and cosmic reset.
cross_tradition_parallels: Aztec fifth sun (current age, ending in earthquakes)

cosmological_frameworks.scholarly_note: Traditional yuga lengths come from the Manusmriti and Puranas; Sri Yukteswar in 'The Holy Science' (1894) proposed a much shorter alternative cycle of 24,000 years. The traditional lengths are symbolic-cosmological; the shorter cycle attempts a historical correlation. Both are present in modern Hindu thought.
cosmological_frameworks.structural_role: The yuga cycle is the Hindu cosmological framework for what other traditions express through linear apocalyptic time (Christian, Zoroastrian) or through repeating cosmic resets (Aztec suns, Stoic ekpyrosis). All three address the same question: how does the current degraded condition relate to a remembered or anticipated uncorrupted state?

cosmological_frameworks.name: Origins of Evil — Gen 6:1-4 Reception History
cosmological_frameworks.summary: A reception-history framework for the Second Temple Jewish, early Christian, Gnostic, and Manichaean tradition that grounds the existence of evil in the rebellion of the Watchers / sons of God and the resulting hybrid race of giants. Tracks how the cryptic Genesis 6:1-4 passage was developed across two millennia into a full cosmological account of why the world is broken.
primary_sources: 1 Enoch 1–36 (Book of the Watchers; chapters 6–11 the core)
Dead Sea Scrolls — esp. Book of Giants (4Q203, 4Q530–533)
Nag Hammadi: On the Origin of the World; Apocryphon of John
Talmud Niddah 61a (Og as grandson of Shemhazai)
Archie T. Wright, The Origin of Evil Spirits (Fortress Press, rev. ed.)
Annette Yoshiko Reed, Fallen Angels and the History of Judaism and Christianity (Cambridge, 2005)
Joseph Lumpkin, Fallen Angels, the Watchers, and the Origins of Evil (popular synthesis)
G.A.G. Stroumsa, Another Seed: Studies in Gnostic Mythology (Leiden, 1984)

core_narrative_strands.summary: 200 angels under Shemhazai descend on Mt Hermon, take human wives, beget giants (Nephilim) who consume creation.

Asael (later Azazel) descends and teaches forbidden arts — metallurgy/weapons to men, cosmetics/sorcery to women — corrupting humanity through technology rather than (or in addition to) interbreeding.

The Nephilim consume crops, then animals, then men, then each other. Their spirits, after their bodies die in the flood, become the demons of the present age (1 Enoch 15) — the standard Second Temple explanation of demon-possession.
God commands the loyal angels to warn Noah, destroy the giants, and bind the Watchers in the earth until the final judgment.
The Nephilim line survives (Numbers 13:33) into the post-flood giant complex — Rephaim, Anakim, Emim, Zamzummim, Og of Bashan, Goliath. The cosmic rebellion has a continuous historical body.

In Gnostic literature (Apocryphon of John, On the Origin of the World) the Watchers become Yaldabaoth's archonic enforcers — the Demiurge's seven planetary rulers — and their forbidden teachings are the chains of material captivity.
Manichaeism keeps the Watcher-teaching motif: the Watchers reveal heavenly mysteries to humanity, but in a form that entangles rather than liberates (Kephalaia 92).

cross_tradition_parallels.parallel: Prometheus's gift of fire / forbidden arts to humanity, leading to the chained punishment of the gift-giver. The structural inversion of the Asael cycle — Prometheus is honored, Asael condemned, for similar acts.

The Dānavas and Daityas (Asuras) descended from Kashyapa-rishi through Dānu and Diti — a giant-warrior-race of divine-mortal mixed parentage repeatedly defeated by the devas. Maya Dānava the master-architect parallels Asael the teacher-of-forbidden-arts.
The Fomorians — chthonic giants defeated at Mag Tuired so the cultivated order can be established.
The apkallu — antediluvian wise beings — and the older gods slain by Marduk. The Watchers-as-teachers-of-arts inherit the apkallu pattern.

The rpum cult of Bashan / Mt Hermon: same territory as the Watcher-descent in 1 Enoch 6, with ancestral warrior-shades summoned for blessing. The 'origins of evil' framework reads the rpum cult itself as part of the giant-line legacy.

cosmological_frameworks.interpretive_significance: This framework is the alternative answer — within Judeo-Christian tradition — to the Adam-and-Eve account of evil's origin. Where Genesis 3 locates evil in human disobedience, the Watcher tradition locates it in angelic rebellion and the technological/biological corruption of humanity from above. The two accounts coexisted in Second Temple Judaism; rabbinic Judaism and Pauline Christianity largely suppressed the Watcher account in favor of the Adamic; Gnostic and Manichaean traditions developed the Watcher account into full cosmologies of cosmic captivity. For comparative purposes the Watcher framework is the bridge that connects the biblical Anakim / Rephaim / Nephilim to the IE / Vedic / Canaanite parallel complexes.

cosmological_frameworks.name: The Global Giants Complex
cosmological_frameworks.summary: A meta-framework that catalogs the worldwide pattern of giant-clan / elder-race traditions. The recurring structure: a prior race, larger and/or older than humans, dominant in an earlier age, ultimately destroyed or overthrown for moral failure or cosmic necessity, leaving traces in the form of megalithic ruins, oversized bones, and the toponymic landscape. The same pattern appears in cultures with no plausible historical contact, raising the comparative-mythology question of whether the pattern reflects (a) a shared psychological/archetypal substrate, (b) common observation of megafaunal fossils and prior megalithic civilizations, (c) diffusion from a common source, or (d) all three.

named_individuals: The 20 Watcher chiefs (Semyaza, Azazel, Araqiel, Kokabiel, Sariel, etc.)

key_sources: Egyptian Execration Texts (Middle Kingdom, c. 19th–18th c. BCE; Berlin and Brussels collections)

primary_terms: the older gods slain by Marduk

named_individuals: Otus and Ephialtes (Gigantes who piled Pelion on Ossa)

key_sources: Alva Ixtlilxochitl's Historia de la Nación Chichimeca

primary_terms: the first inhabitants of Earth (in various Inca traditions)
Oka Nahullo ('white people of the water')
key_sources: Various tribal oral traditions; collected ethnographies

primary_terms: Kua Fu (the chaser of the sun)

key_sources: Various local Japanese traditions and folk-tales

primary_terms: Various regional giants in Nigerian and other African folklore
key_sources: Yoruba oral tradition; various African folk-traditions

structural_features_present_across_tradi: Elder, larger race predating present humanity
Divine or semi-divine parentage (often via interbreeding)
Teachers of forbidden arts (more specific to Levantine cluster)
Sins or pride leading to destruction
Destruction by flood / fire / cosmic cataclysm / war
Bones / remains attested in landscape (often the megafaunal-fossil-misidentification explanation)
Toponymic preservation (Bashan, Cholula, Lovelock Cave, etc.)
Imprisonment of a key figure to await final judgment
scholarly_frameworks: Adrienne Mayor, Fossil Legends of the First Americans (2005) — argues many giant traditions worldwide originate in encounters with megafaunal fossils
Loren T. Stuckenbruck, The Book of Giants from Qumran (1997)
Annette Yoshiko Reed, Fallen Angels and the History of Judaism and Christianity (2005)
Calvert Watkins, How to Kill a Dragon (1995) — for the dragon-slayer pattern as separate-but-related
Bruce Lincoln, 'The Indo-European Myth of Creation' (1975) — for the Yemo-sacrifice pattern
G.A.G. Stroumsa, Another Seed: Studies in Gnostic Mythology (1984)
Mark S. Smith, The Origins of Biblical Monotheism (2001)
cosmological_frameworks.interpretive_significance: The global giants complex is the strongest single piece of evidence for cross-cultural mythological pattern, regardless of which explanation one prefers. Even if all instances are entirely independent, the convergence on a single structural pattern (elder race, divine mixing, sin, cataclysm, ruins-and-bones-as-evidence) across cultures separated by oceans and millennia indicates that the human imagination is constrained to a small set of possible stories about its own deep past. For the 'Parallels of the Gods' project this is the spinal column.

cosmological_frameworks.name: The Dragon-Slayer Formula (*eghent oghim — he slew the serpent)
cosmological_frameworks.summary: Calvert Watkins (How to Kill a Dragon, 1995) identified a specific verbal formula across IE languages: the hero slays the serpent/dragon. The formula reconstructs to PIE *eghent oghim ('he slew the serpent'). Attestations: Vedic Indra slays Vritra; Greek Apollo slays Python; Norse Thor slays Jörmungandr; Slavic Perun slays Veles; Hittite Tarhunt slays Illuyankas; Germanic Beowulf slays Grendel's Mother; Hebrew Yahweh slays Leviathan/Rahab; Japanese Susanoo slays Yamata-no-Orochi; Babylonian Marduk slays Tiamat.

stages.name: The Hero (Storm-God or Hero-Figure)
stages.character: The protagonist is typically a thunder-god or champion-hero who wields a weapon associated with storm / lightning / the sky-realm.

stages.name: The Serpent / Dragon
stages.character: The adversary is typically serpentine, chthonic, waterbound, or chaos-associated. Often blocks the waters (drought formula) or hoards treasure.

stages.name: The Weapon
stages.character: Thunderbolt, hammer, spear, or lightning-associated weapon. Sometimes won or made for the specific purpose of slaying the serpent.
cross_tradition_parallels: Susanoo's sword Kusanagi (found in the dragon)

stages.name: The Release of the Waters / Restoration of Order
stages.character: The serpent's defeat releases the blocked waters, restores the stolen cattle, or establishes cosmic order. The act of slaying is cosmogonic.
cross_tradition_parallels: Indra releases the rains after slaying Vritra
Apollo establishes the Delphic oracle at Python's site
Marduk uses Tiamat's body to make the cosmos
Susanoo finds the Kusanagi sword (one of three Sacred Treasures)

cosmological_frameworks.scholarly_note: Calvert Watkins, How to Kill a Dragon: Aspects of Indo-European Poetics (Oxford, 1995) is the foundational treatment. The formula is linguistic as well as mythological — the verbal phrase for slaying the serpent is directly reconstructible in PIE. West's Indo-European Poetry and Myth (Oxford, 2007) extends the analysis. The formula applies strictly to IE traditions; analogous dragon-slayer myths in non-IE traditions (Mesopotamian, Japanese) are parallel structures with different historical origins.
cosmological_frameworks.structural_role: The dragon-slayer formula is the most concretely documented cross-tradition mythic pattern in comparative mythology — documentable at the linguistic level, not just the thematic level. It connects: Indra, Thor, Apollo, Perun, Marduk, Yahweh (as Leviathan-slayer), Susanoo, and St. George / Michael in one structural family. The 'hero-slays-chaos-serpent' pattern is the PIE root of what later traditions call 'the triumph of order over chaos.'

cosmological_frameworks.name: The Dying-and-Rising God Formula (Frazer → Critical Reception)
cosmological_frameworks.summary: James George Frazer's The Golden Bough (1890–1915) proposed a universal 'dying-and-rising god' pattern: a deity dies and is resurrected, associated with agricultural cycles. Frazer grouped: Osiris, Tammuz, Adonis, Attis, Dionysus, Persephone, Balder, Christ. Jonathan Z. Smith's 1987 article 'Dying and Rising Gods' (in Encyclopedia of Religion) challenged the universality — many cases are 'disappearing gods' (not dying) or 'dying but not truly rising' or 'descending and returning.' The pattern is real but more precise than Frazer claimed. The Source Map presents both the Frazerian synthesis and Smith's critique.

stages.name: Death / Descent / Disappearance
stages.character: The deity dies violently, descends to the underworld, or disappears from the world of the living. The cosmos suffers without them.
cross_tradition_parallels: Osiris murdered by Set and scattered (Egyptian)
Tammuz / Dumuzi taken to the underworld by demons (Sumerian)
Dionysus-Zagreus torn apart by the Titans (Orphic Greek)
Inanna descends through the seven gates (Sumerian)
Balder slain by the mistletoe arrow (Norse)
Attis self-castrated and died under a pine (Phrygian)

stages.name: The Cosmic Suffering
stages.character: While the deity is absent, the world suffers — crops fail, fertility ceases, death spreads, or light disappears.
cross_tradition_parallels: Demeter's grief causes crops to fail (Greek)
Inanna's absence causes sexuality to cease among all creatures (Sumerian)
Amaterasu's cave causes darkness to fall (Japanese)

stages.name: Recovery / Resurrection / Return
stages.character: The deity is recovered, reassembled, revived, or returns from the dead / underworld.
cross_tradition_parallels: Geshtinanna agrees to substitute for Dumuzi half the year (Sumerian)
Christ rises on the third day (Christian)
Dionysus's heart rescued by Athena, reborn (Orphic Greek)

stages.name: Smith's Corrective: Disappearing vs. Dying
stages.character: Jonathan Z. Smith notes that many figures in this category do not truly 'die and rise' — they disappear and return (Persephone, Inanna) or die without true resurrection (Osiris becomes king of the dead but does not return to life). The precision matters.
cross_tradition_parallels: Truly dying and rising: Christ (Christian), Dionysus-Zagreus (Orphic)
Descending and returning: Persephone, Inanna, Ishtar
Dying but becoming king of dead: Osiris

cosmological_frameworks.scholarly_note: Frazer, The Golden Bough (1890–1915, 12 vols.) — the origin of the category. Jonathan Z. Smith, 'Dying and Rising Gods,' Encyclopedia of Religion (1987) — the definitive scholarly challenge to Frazer's universalism. Mark S. Smith, The Origins of Biblical Monotheism (Oxford, 2001) — Ugaritic / Baal cycle. Tryggve Mettinger, The Riddle of Resurrection (Almqvist, 2001) — defends a limited form of the category against Smith. The debate is ongoing; both positions are represented here.
cosmological_frameworks.structural_role: The dying-and-rising-god pattern is the most contested major category in comparative religion — proposed by Frazer as universal, challenged by Smith as over-generalized. The Source Map notes: the pattern IS real but the mechanism differs. Christ's resurrection (unique, bodily, historical claim), Osiris's transformation (becomes underworld king, not restored to life), and Persephone's seasonal descent (never truly died) are structurally different even if thematically similar. This distinction is tracked in the evidence-type field: structural-function-match vs. documented-historical-transmission.
